definition_en: a country or its government, a region within a country, a condition, or to say something formally
core_image: 地图上一个有边界的国家
scene: 这个国家重视教育。 The state invests in education.
sceneCN: 这里 state 是「国家」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这个国家重视教育。

senses.title: Country and government
senses.definition: a country together with its government
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家及其政府
senses.example: The state invests in education.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家重视教育。
senses.why: A political country is the oldest public sense.
senses.whyCN: 政治意义上的国家，是最古老的公共义项。

senses.title: Region of a country
senses.definition: a region within a country that has its own government
senses.definitionCN: 一国内拥有自己政府的地区
senses.example: Texas is a large state.
senses.exampleCN: 得克萨斯是一个大州。
senses.why: A federal country divides itself into states.
senses.whyCN: 联邦制国家把自己划分为州。

senses.title: Condition
senses.definition: the condition that someone or something is in
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某物所处的状况
senses.example: The patient is in a stable state.
senses.exampleCN: 病人处于稳定状态。
senses.why: A standing condition is the Latin core of the word.
senses.whyCN: 「站立着的状况」，是这个词的拉丁语核心。

senses.title: Say formally
senses.definition: to say or write something in a clear, formal way
senses.definitionCN: 以清晰正式的方式说出或写出某事
senses.example: Please state your name.
senses.exampleCN: 请说出你的姓名。
senses.why: The noun of a condition became a verb of setting out.
senses.whyCN: 表示状况的名词，转为把事情摆出来的动词。

intro.en: State comes from Latin status, a standing or condition, through Old French estat.
intro.cn: state 经古法语 estat 来自拉丁语 status（站立；状况）。

items.en: Status meant a standing or condition.
items.cn: status 意为站立或状况。

items.en: Estat named a rank or a condition.
items.cn: estat 指等级或状况。

items.en: State meant a condition and an estate.
items.cn: state 指状况，也指产业。

items.en: It named a political country.
items.cn: 它开始指政治意义上的国家。

items.en: The verb sense of stating facts grew.
items.cn: 「陈述事实」的动词义发展起来。

note.en: State is compared with look-alike words and words for countries or conditions.
note.cn: 把 state 与形近词以及表示国家或状况的词作比较。

definition_zh: 鬼；幽灵；幽灵般的人；隐约的一点；替写他人作品的人（作动词）
definition_en: the spirit of a dead person that some people believe they can see, or something faint and vague like such a spirit
core_image: 夜里的白影：一缕看不见身体的人形浮在旧屋里
scene: 老房子的走廊尽头，孩子说看见一团白影一闪而过。 The children said a ghost walked along the corridor of the old house.
sceneCN: 这里 ghost 是「鬼；幽灵」（第 1 个义项：死者的灵魂显现）；句意为孩子们说一个幽灵在老房子的走廊里走过。

derivatives.zh: 由 ghost 加 -ly 构成，义为「幽灵般的；可怕的」
由 ghost 加 -like 构成，义为「像鬼一样的」
由 ghost 加 -ing 构成，义为「忽然断联；淡出式失联」

senses.title: The spirit of a dead person
senses.definition: the spirit of a dead person that people believe appears to the living
senses.definitionCN: 人们相信会向活人显现的死者的灵魂
senses.example: She claimed she saw a ghost in the attic.
senses.exampleCN: 她说她在阁楼上看见了幽灵。
senses.why: The core image is a visible person-shape without a body, so the oldest sense is the departed soul that still walks.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是「有人的形状却没有身体」，所以最早的义项就是仍在走动的死者灵魂。

senses.title: A faint trace of something
senses.definition: a very small amount or weak trace of something, often following 'the ghost of'
senses.definitionCN: 某物极小的一点或微弱残迹，常用于「the ghost of」结构
senses.example: There was not the ghost of a chance of winning.
senses.exampleCN: 连一丝获胜的机会都没有。
senses.why: A ghost is barely there, so English extends it to anything so faint it is almost nothing.
senses.whyCN: 鬼影似有似无，英语便用它指微弱到几乎不存在的痕迹。

senses.title: A ghostwriter
senses.definition: a writer whose work is officially credited to another person
senses.definitionCN: 作品署名为他人、实际代写的作者
senses.example: He worked as a ghost for two famous politicians.
senses.exampleCN: 他曾为两位著名政治人物代笔。
senses.why: The written text appears under one name but the invisible hand of another shaped it, like a hidden spirit.
senses.whyCN: 文字署着一个人的名字，却由一只看不见的手写成，就像隐形的幽灵。

senses.title: To ghostwrite
senses.definition: to write a book or article for someone else who is named as the author
senses.definitionCN: 替署名作者撰写书籍或文章
senses.example: She ghosted three novels before publishing her own name.
senses.exampleCN: 她代写了三部小说之后才用自己的名字出版。
senses.why: The verb grows from the hidden-writer sense: the real author stays unseen like a spirit.
senses.whyCN: 动词从「隐形写手」义项生长而来：真正的作者像幽灵一样不被看见。

senses.title: A faint image or echo
senses.definition: a faint secondary image or an unwanted faint signal or echo
senses.definitionCN: 微弱的次级影像或多余的低弱信号、回声
senses.example: The old film print left ghost images on the screen.
senses.exampleCN: 老旧的电影胶片在银幕上留下了残影。
senses.why: A ghost image is a weak copy of something stronger, keeping the idea of a barely visible form.
senses.whyCN: 残像是强影像的微弱副本，保留了「似有似无的形状」这一意象。

intro.en: Ghost is one of the oldest words in English, running straight back to the Germanic spirit-word.
intro.cn: ghost 是英语里最古老的词之一，直接追溯到日耳曼语的「灵魂」一词。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic root gheustoz meant spirit or breath.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼词根 gheustoz 意为灵魂或气息。

items.en: Old English gast meant spirit, soul, breath, and also a frightening apparition.
items.cn: 古英语 gast 意为灵魂、气息，也指吓人的鬼怪显现。

items.en: Norse gaver and related forms reinforced the Germanic family in northern England.
items.cn: 诺斯语的 gaver 等相关形式加强了英格兰北部的这一日耳曼词族。

items.en: Middle English spelled it gost or goost; the h appeared later under Flemish influence.
items.cn: 中古英语拼作 gost 或 goost；字母 h 后来受佛兰芒语影响才加入。

items.en: Modern English fixed the spelling ghost; Holy Ghost survives as a religious term for the Holy Spirit.
items.cn: 现代英语定为 ghost；Holy Ghost 作为圣灵的宗教用语留存至今。

note.en: The words below share ghost's sound or its spirit-family of meanings.
note.cn: 下面的词与 ghost 音近，或同属「灵魂、显现」的义场。

entries.definition: Ghost-like in appearance; pale and frightening.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「幽灵般的；惨白可怕的」，由 ghost 直接派生。

entries.definition: A person staying at your home; only one letter different.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「客人」，拼写与 ghost 仅差一个字母，词源不同。

entries.definition: An evil spirit that robs graves in Arabic folklore; sounds close to ghost.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「食尸鬼」，源于阿拉伯民间传说，读音接近 ghost。

entries.definition: The non-physical part of a person, or a supernatural being.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「灵魂；神灵」，比 ghost 更宽泛，可指人的精神。

entries.definition: A ghost or something seen that is not real.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「幻影；幽灵」，偏书面，也指虚幻之物。

entries.definition: A ghost, especially a frightening one; British spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「鬼怪；萦绕心头的恐惧」，英式拼写，美式作 specter。

normalIntro.en: Five links to real forms and uses of ghost.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实构形与用法的联想。

normal.en: Old English gast meant breath as well as soul, since breathing is the sign of life.
normal.cn: 古英语 gast 既指灵魂也指气息，因为呼吸是生命的标志。

normal.en: The h in ghost arrived from Flemish typesetters, so the spelling is later than the sound.
normal.cn: ghost 的 h 来自佛兰芒排字工，拼写比读音晚出现。

normal.en: Holy Ghost still names the Holy Spirit in Christian texts.
normal.cn: 基督教文本仍用 Holy Ghost 指圣灵。

normal.en: A ghost writer is the invisible author behind a famous name.
normal.cn: ghost writer 是名人之名背后看不见的作者。

normal.en: Ghost town is a town whose people have all gone, leaving empty streets.
normal.cn: ghost town 指居民全部离开、街道空荡的废城。

abstract.en: Picture a white shape in a dark corridor: it has a person's outline but no face.
abstract.cn: 想象黑走廊里一团白影：有人的轮廓却没有脸。

abstract.en: Think of a cold spot in a warm room where something unseen stands.
abstract.cn: 想象温暖的房间里有一处冷点，那里站着看不见的东西。

abstract.en: See a thin echo of a smile that disappears when you look straight at it.
abstract.cn: 想象一抹若有若无的微笑，你直视它时它就消失。

examples.en: The children said a ghost walked along the corridor of the old house.
examples.cn: 孩子们说一个幽灵在老房子的走廊里走过。

examples.en: He worked as a ghost for two famous politicians.
examples.cn: 他曾为两位著名政治人物代笔。

examples.en: There was not the ghost of a chance of winning.
examples.cn: 连一丝获胜的机会都没有。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「够死特」——鬼魂够吓人，死去的灵魂特别地出现；ghost 让人想起黑屋里的白影

root: ghost 源自日耳曼语词根 gheustoz（灵魂、气息），经古英语 gast 直传至今；与德语 Geist（精神）同源，词族纯属日耳曼，与拉丁 spiritus 无关。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of ghost keeps the same picture: something present in shape but absent in body.
sensesIntro.cn: ghost 的每个义项都保留同一画面：有形无实的存在。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person-shape with no body, faintly visible
core.cn: 核心意象：有人的轮廓却没有身体、隐约可见的存在

branches.en: the soul that returns
branches.cn: 死者的灵魂回访人间

branches.en: the almost-nothing trace
branches.cn: 微弱到几乎不存在的痕迹或回声

branches.en: the writer behind the name
branches.cn: 署名背后隐形的写作者

branches.en: the pale frightening figure
branches.cn: 惨白吓人的身影

branches.en: the doubled faint image
branches.cn: 影像的重影与残像

intro.cn: ghost 是日耳曼基础词，下面列出它自身的词尾和构成的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin has spiritus for breath and soul; it is a parallel tradition, not the source of ghost.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语以 spiritus 表示气息与灵魂，是与日耳曼传统平行的体系，并非 ghost 的来源。

items.example: Old English gast covered both soul and monster.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 gast 兼指灵魂与怪影。

definition_zh: 火车；列车；一系列；随从；（作动词）训练；培养
definition_en: a line of connected railway carriages pulled by an engine, or a connected series of things; and to teach or practise a skill
core_image: 一节车厢连着一节车厢，由前面的机车拉着往前走
scene: 站台上的人把箱子往前挪了挪，远处一列长长的车正慢慢地收住速度。 The train pulled into the station exactly on time.
sceneCN: 这里 train 是「火车、列车」（第 1 个义项：由机车牵引的一列车厢）；句意为那列火车准点驶进了车站。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「训练；培训」
由动词加 -ee 构成，义为「受训者」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「教练；训练者」

senses.title: Railway carriages pulled by an engine
senses.definition: a line of railway carriages or wagons joined together and pulled by an engine
senses.definitionCN: 由机车牵引、首尾相连的一列铁路车厢
senses.example: The night train to the coast leaves at ten.
senses.exampleCN: 去海边的夜车十点发车。
senses.why: The French source means something dragged along, and a train is literally a line of things dragged behind an engine.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源意为被拖着的东西，而火车字面上就是一串被拖在机车后面的东西。

senses.title: A connected series of things
senses.definition: a sequence of events, ideas, or objects that follow one after another
senses.definitionCN: 一个接一个相继发生的事件、想法或物件
senses.example: The news broke his train of thought completely.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息把他的思路彻底打断了。
senses.why: A line of carriages is the model for any line of things, so the word becomes a general word for series.
senses.whyCN: 一串车厢是任何一串事物的模型，于是这个词成为泛指「系列」的词。

senses.title: The followers of an important person
senses.definition: a group of servants or attendants travelling behind a person of rank
senses.definitionCN: 跟在显贵身后同行的一群仆从或随员
senses.example: The queen arrived with a train of forty attendants.
senses.exampleCN: 女王带着四十名随从到来。
senses.why: People following in order are dragged behind in a line, just as carriages are, so the word covers a retinue.
senses.whyCN: 按次序跟着的人正如车厢一样被拖成一列，所以这个词也指随行队伍。

senses.title: The long back part of a dress
senses.definition: the long part of a formal dress or robe that drags behind the wearer
senses.definitionCN: 礼服或长袍身后拖地的长摆
senses.example: Two children carried the bride's train up the steps.
senses.exampleCN: 两个孩子把新娘的裙裾提上台阶。
senses.why: The dragging part of a garment is the most physical remnant of the original dragging sense.
senses.whyCN: 衣袍被拖着的部分，是原始「拖」义最具体的遗留。

senses.title: To teach and practise a skill
senses.definition: to teach a person or animal a skill through repeated practice
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复练习教人或动物掌握某项技能
senses.example: She trains new staff for six weeks before they start.
senses.exampleCN: 新员工上岗前她培训他们六周。
senses.why: From dragging things in a line comes the idea of leading someone along a course, and so of forming them by practice.
senses.whyCN: 从把事物拖成一列，发展出把人带着走完一段课程的想法，于是形成「以练习培养」之义。

senses.title: To prepare for a contest
senses.definition: to exercise and practise regularly in order to be ready for a sport or event
senses.definitionCN: 为备战某项运动或赛事而定期锻炼练习
senses.example: He trains in the pool every morning at six.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天早上六点在泳池里训练。
senses.why: The person being formed by practice can also form himself, so the verb becomes intransitive.
senses.whyCN: 被练习塑造的人也可以自己塑造自己，于是这个动词有了不及物用法。

intro.en: Train comes from Old French trahiner, to drag, from Latin trahere, to pull; the sense of a railway train dates from the 1820s.
intro.cn: train 来自古法语 trahiner（拖），源自拉丁语 trahere（拉）；表示火车的意思始于十九世纪二十年代。

items.en: Trahere means to pull or drag, and its stem underlies a large family in English.
items.cn: 拉丁语 trahere 意为拉、拖，其词干在英语中撑起一个大家族。

items.en: Trahiner means to drag along, and the noun train means something dragged or a line of things.
items.cn: 古法语 trahiner 意为沿地拖，名词 train 意为被拖之物或一列东西。

items.en: English borrows train for a trailing part, a retinue, and a sequence of events.
items.cn: 英语借入 train，指拖尾部分、随从以及一连串事件。

items.en: With the railways of the 1820s the word settles on the line of carriages, which becomes its dominant sense.
items.cn: 十九世纪二十年代铁路出现后，这个词固定在「一列车厢」上，成为其主要含义。

items.en: The verb to train, meaning to bring a person or animal along by practice, is older and grows in use with armies and schools.
items.cn: 动词 train 意为通过练习把人或动物培养出来，这一用法更早，并随军队与学校的发展而增多。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the -ing, -ee, and -er forms, while the near-meaning group gathers rail terms and teaching words.
note.cn: 形近组收集 -ing、-ee、-er 等形式，近义组收集铁路术语与教学类词。

normalIntro.cn: 「拖」的原义、常用搭配以及 -ing、-ee、-er 词族入手。

normal.en: A train is a line of things dragged along, so the carriages and the dress train are the same picture.
normal.cn: 火车是一串被拖着走的东西，所以车厢与裙裾是同一幅画面。

normal.cn: train of thought，想法像车厢一样一节接一节。

normal.en: Training is the activity, a trainee is the person learning, a trainer is the person teaching.
normal.cn: training 是活动，trainee 是学习的人，trainer 是教的人。

normal.en: By train, catch a train, miss a train: the transport sense takes articles freely.
normal.cn: by train、catch a train、miss a train，交通义可以自由加冠词。

normal.en: To train is to walk someone along a course until the skill sticks.
normal.cn: to train 就是带着某人走完一段课程，直到技能定型。

abstract.en: Picture a long dark line of carriages curving into the station.
abstract.cn: 想象一列深色车厢弯进车站的长长的样子。

abstract.en: Think of a queen's long robe held up by two children on stone steps.
abstract.cn: 想女王的长袍在两个孩子的搀扶下走过石阶。

abstract.en: A train is a plan made of steel, always arriving before its own end.
abstract.cn: 火车是用钢做成的计划，总在自己终点之前先到站。

examples.en: We took the early train to the city.
examples.cn: 我们坐早班车进城。

examples.en: The letter broke my train of thought.
examples.cn: 这封信打断了我的思路。

examples.en: The dogs are trained to search for people in snow.
examples.cn: 这些狗受过在雪中寻人的训练。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扯你」——前面机车一扯，后面的车厢全跟着走，就是一列车。

root: 拉丁语 trahere（拉、拖）→ 古法语 trahiner（沿地拖）→ 中古英语 train（拖尾、随从、序列）→ 近代英语 train（列车；训练）。词族有 training、trainee、trainer。

sensesIntro.en: Everything starts from dragging: the dragged line gives carriages and dress trains, the line of followers gives a retinue, the line of events gives a series, and the leading of people along a course gives the verb to train.
sensesIntro.cn: 一切都从拖拽开始：被拖的线给出车厢与裙裾，跟成一列的人给出随从，排成一串的事件给出系列，而带着人走完课程则给出动词「训练」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of connected things pulled along in order.
core.cn: 核心意象：一串相连之物依序被拉着前行。

branches.en: The railway train.
branches.cn: 铁路列车。

branches.en: Any series in a line.
branches.cn: 任何成串的序列。

branches.en: Followers in line and cloth dragged behind.
branches.cn: 排成一列的随从与身后的拖布。

branches.en: Leading someone along a course of practice.
branches.cn: 带着人走完练习的课程。

branches.en: The learner's own repeated practice.
branches.cn: 学习者自身的反复练习。

intro.en: The word is a French borrowing from the Latin pulling verb, and its family uses -ing, -ee, and -er.
intro.cn: 本词是经法语借入的拉丁「拉」动词词族，其词族使用 -ing、-ee、-er。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pulling verb and its participle are the base of this family and of many prefixed relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁「拉」动词及其分词是这个词族以及众多前缀词的根基。

items.example: The stem underlies train, trait, and attract.
A trainee is the one being trained.
Trained staff are not easy to replace.
items.exampleCN: 受过训的员工不易替换。

items.example: A rail train runs on steel lines.
items.exampleCN: rail train 在钢轨上行驶。

items.example: A train of thought is a series of ideas.
items.exampleCN: train of thought 是一串想法。

items.example: A train station is where the cars stop.
items.exampleCN: train station 是车厢停下的地方。

definition_zh: 介绍；引进；提出；开始
definition_en: to tell people someone's name, to bring something in for the first time, or to begin something
core_image: 一个人牵着另一个人的手，把他领进一间坐满陌生人的屋子
scene: 晚宴开始时，主人走到客人身边，把他们两两凑在一起说名字。 They introduced the new system last spring.
sceneCN: 这里 introduce 是「引进、推行」（第 2 个义项：把新事物带入使用），句意为他们去年春天引进了这套新系统。画面里的物件：晚宴长桌、香槟杯、贴着新标签的控制台。

pos.zh: 动词：介绍；引进；提出；作为……的开头

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -tion 构成，义为「介绍；引进；前言」
由本词加 -ory 构成，义为「引导性的；入门的」
由本词截短构成，义为「引言；开场」
同出 duc- 词根，义为「教育的」

senses.title: Make two people known
senses.definition: to tell two people each other's names so that they can begin to know each other
senses.definitionCN: 说出两人的名字，使他们可以开始相识
senses.example: Let me introduce my sister before we sit down.
senses.exampleCN: 坐下之前让我介绍一下我妹妹。
senses.why: Latin ducere means to lead; intro- means inward. To introduce is to lead someone in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ducere 意为「引导」，intro- 意为「向内」，introduce 就是把人领进来。

senses.title: Bring something in
senses.definition: to bring a new thing, idea, or rule into use for the first time
senses.definitionCN: 首次把新事物、新想法或新规定投入使用
senses.example: The school introduced a later start for older pupils.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为高年级学生推出了更晚的到校时间。
senses.why: The leading-in picture suits ideas too: new rules are walked into a system.
senses.whyCN: 「领进来」的图像也适用于想法：新规定被领进一个体系。

senses.title: Become familiar with
senses.definition: to cause someone to experience or learn about something for the first time
senses.definitionCN: 使某人第一次接触或了解某事物
senses.example: Her aunt introduced her to jazz when she was ten.
senses.exampleCN: 她十岁时，姑母带她第一次接触爵士乐。
senses.why: Here the person is led into a subject as if into a room.
senses.whyCN: 这里人是被领进一门学问，就像被领进一间屋子。

senses.title: Begin a piece
senses.definition: to begin a speech, book, or programme with something
senses.definitionCN: 用某内容作为演讲、书籍或节目的开头
senses.example: The chair introduced the meeting with two minutes of thanks.
senses.exampleCN: 主席用两分钟致谢作为会议的开场。
senses.why: Opening a meeting is leading the audience in, so the same verb serves.
senses.whyCN: 会议开场就是把听众领进来，所以还是用同一个动词。

intro.en: Introduce joins Latin intro- "inward" and ducere "to lead": to lead someone in.
intro.cn: introduce 把拉丁语 intro-「向内」与 ducere「引导」结合：把人领进来。

items.en: Ducere meant to lead or draw along.
items.cn: ducere 意为带领或牵引。

items.en: Introducere meant to lead a person or thing inside.
items.cn: introducere 意为把人或物领进去。

items.en: French introduire kept the ceremonial sense of bringing someone in.
items.cn: 法语 introduire 保留了把人带进来的礼仪义。

items.en: English used introduce for presenting a person at court or at home.
items.cn: 英语用 introduce 指在宫廷或家中引见某人。

items.en: Industry and law added the sense of putting a new thing into use.
items.cn: 工业与法律又添上「把新事物投入使用」义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -duce leading root; the near-meaning group holds other words for presenting.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -duce「引导」词根；近义组收其他表示「推出」的词。

entries.definition: The act or the opening section that results.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「介绍；引言」。

entries.definition: To lead something back or make it smaller.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「减少」，同出 ducere。

entries.definition: To lead something forward into being.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「生产」，同出 ducere。

entries.definition: To show or hand over something formally.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「呈现；呈交」，更正式。

entries.definition: To start using something new.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语义为「引入」，偏口语。

entries.definition: To start a product or campaign publicly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「推出；发起」，强调公开。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the picture of a hand leading another person indoors.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子守着「一只手把别人领进屋里」的画面。

normal.en: intro- inward plus duc lead equals lead in.
normal.cn: intro-「向内」加 duc「引导」等于「领进来」。

normal.en: The same duc root appears in reduce, produce, and conduct.
normal.cn: 同一个 duc 词根出现在 reduce、produce、conduct 里。

normal.en: Introduce yourself is the shortest formal speech you will give.
normal.cn: introduce yourself 是你要讲的最短的正式发言。

normal.en: Schools introduce rules the way hosts introduce guests.
normal.cn: 学校推行规定，就像主人介绍客人。

normal.en: Her aunt introduced her to jazz: led her into a room of sound.
normal.cn: 姑母带她认识爵士：把她领进一间装满声音的屋子。

abstract.en: To introduce is to open a door and stand aside.
abstract.cn: 介绍就是打开一扇门，然后退到一边。

abstract.en: New ideas also need someone to walk them in.
abstract.cn: 新想法也需要有人牵着走进去。

abstract.en: The word is a handshake turned into grammar.
abstract.cn: 这个词是把一次握手写成了语法。

examples.en: She introduced me to her old teacher at the gate.
examples.cn: 她在门口把我介绍给了她的老师。

examples.en: The company introduced a shorter working week.
examples.cn: 公司推行了更短的工作周。

examples.en: He introduced his talk with a story about his father.
examples.cn: 他用一个关于父亲的故事开了讲座的头。

dict_mnemonic.text: intro（向内）+ duce（引导）——把人领进门

root: 拉丁语 intro「向内」+ ducere「引导」→ introducere「领进去」→ 古法语 introduire → 英语 introduce。同族有 introduction、introductory、produce。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: make people known, bring something new in, lead someone into a subject, and open a piece.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：让人相识、引进新事物、带人入门，以及作为开场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand leading another person through a doorway.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手牵着另一个人穿过门口。

branches.en: THE NAMES: two strangers given to each other.
branches.cn: 名字这条线：两个陌生人被交给彼此。

branches.en: THE RULE: a new practice led into a system.
branches.cn: 规定这条线：新做法被领进一个体系。

branches.en: THE RECORD: a young listener led into jazz.
branches.cn: 唱片这条线：年轻听者被领进爵士。

branches.en: THE PODIUM: an opening line that leads the audience in.
branches.cn: 讲台这条线：把听众领进来的开场白。

branches.en: THE LINK: both senses bring someone into a place they did not know.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都把某人带进他原本不认识的地方。

intro.en: Introduce is intro- "inward" plus the root duc- "lead" with the verb ending.
intro.cn: introduce 是 intro-「向内」加词根 duc-「引导」与动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere, introducere and the participle introductus are recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ducere、introducere 与分词 introductus 均有记载。

items.example: It marks the direction of leading.
The root also appears in conduct and educate.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 conduct 与 educate。

items.example: The verb is the base of the root.
The verb is the direct source.
It forms reduce, to lead back.
It forms produce, to lead forth.

definition_zh: 力；力量；力气；武力；强制；效力；部队；人力；迫使
definition_en: physical strength or power, or the power that makes something happen or makes someone act against resistance
core_image: 一根被重物压弯的钢梁架在千斤顶上，梁身一点点被顶回直线
scene: 工地上一根钢梁被落下的重物压弯，工人架起千斤顶，梁身一点点回直。 The jack applied a steady force until the bent beam straightened.
sceneCN: 这里 force 指使物体形状或运动改变的机械推力（第 1 个义项：物理意义上的力）；句意：千斤顶持续施加力，直到弯梁被顶直。图中可辨识物件：千斤顶、弯钢梁、落下的配重、地上的安全帽。

pos.zh: 力；力量；武力；效力；部队；人力
迫使；强行推动；勉强打开

derivatives.zh: 有力的；有说服力的
强有力地
有力；强势
强行的；用武力的
执行；强制实施

senses.title: A push or pull that changes motion
senses.titleCN: 改变运动或形状的推拉力
senses.definition: a physical push or pull that can change the speed, direction or shape of a body
senses.definitionCN: 能改变物体速度、方向或形状的物理推拉作用
senses.example: The net force on the cart equals its mass times its acceleration.
senses.exampleCN: 小车所受的合力等于质量乘以加速度。
senses.why: Latin fortis meant strong, and mechanics took the word for the measurable quantity that makes a body move or bend.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 fortis 意为强壮，力学借这个词来指使物体运动或弯曲的可测之量。

senses.title: Strength of body or blow
senses.definition: muscular strength, or the power carried by a blow, a throw or a wave
senses.definitionCN: 肌肉的力量，或一击、一掷、一道浪所带的威力
senses.example: The force of the wave knocked the swimmer off her feet.
senses.exampleCN: 浪的力量把游泳者掀翻。
senses.why: Before physics existed, force was simply the strength that a body or a blow carries.
senses.whyCN: 在物理学出现之前，force 就是身体或一击所带的力气。

senses.title: Compulsion against resistance
senses.titleCN: 对抵抗施加的强制与武力
senses.definition: the use of pressure or violence to make someone do something against their will
senses.definitionCN: 用压力或暴力使人违背意愿地做某事
senses.example: The door yielded only to force.
senses.exampleCN: 那扇门只有靠强力才被打开。
senses.why: A strong hand can push a person as it pushes a door, so bodily strength became compulsion.
senses.whyCN: 强壮的手能推人，也能推门，于是体力这一义引申为强制。

senses.title: Binding power of law or rule
senses.definition: the legal or formal power that makes a rule, agreement or order binding
senses.definitionCN: 使规则、协议或命令具有约束力的法律或正式效力
senses.example: The new rules came into force at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定在午夜开始生效。
senses.why: A rule in force has the strength of an authority behind it, as if it could push a person into line.
senses.whyCN: 处于生效状态的规则背后有权威的力量，仿佛能把人推回队列。

senses.title: Power to convince
senses.definition: the strength of an argument, feeling or habit to move people's minds or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 论点、情感或习惯打动人心、改变行为的力量
senses.example: The force of her argument silenced the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她论证的力量让全场静了下来。
senses.why: An argument moves a mind the way a hand moves a body, so the same word covers mental pushing.
senses.whyCN: 论证推动人心，正如手推动身体，因此同一个词也指精神上的推力。

senses.title: An armed body of people
senses.definition: an organized body of soldiers, police or other armed personnel
senses.definitionCN: 有组织的军人、警察或其他武装人员群体
senses.example: The peacekeeping force reached the border at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 维和部队在黎明时抵达边境。
senses.why: Strength collected into a unit is spoken of as a force, a collective use of the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 把力量聚成一个单位，就说成一支 force，这是同一名词的集体用法。

senses.title: Manpower counted as a group
senses.definition: the number of people available for work, or a group treated as a single power
senses.definitionCN: 可供工作的人数，或被当作一股力量的人群
senses.example: The factory's labour force grew by a third in two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂的劳动力两年间增加了三分之一。
senses.why: Once force meant strength in numbers, any body of workers could be counted as a force.
senses.whyCN: 当 force 指人数所聚的力量，任何一群工人也能被计为一股 force。

senses.title: To make something happen by pressure
senses.definition: to cause something to happen or to move by using pressure, effort or necessity
senses.definitionCN: 借助压力、努力或情势使某事发生或移动
senses.example: Illness forced him to give up the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 疾病迫使他放弃夜班。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb: to put strength behind something until it yields.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：把力量压到某事背后，直到它让步。

intro.en: Force comes through Old French from late Latin fortia, a plural noun of strength built on fortis 'strong'. The physics sense dates from the seventeenth century, while the military sense is a collective use of the same noun.
intro.cn: force 经古法语来自晚期拉丁 fortia，这是由 fortis「强壮」构成的表「力量」的复数名词。物理义始于十七世纪，军事义则是同一名词的集体用法。

items.en: Fortis meant strong, mighty, able to resist; it described bodies, walls and men alike.
items.cn: fortis 意为强壮、有力量、能抵抗；它既能形容身体，也能形容城墙与人。

items.en: Late Latin fortia, a plural noun built on fortis, named strength or might; it is the form generally cited behind the French word.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 fortia 是由 fortis 构成的复数名词，指力量、威力；一般认为法语词就出自这个形式。

items.en: Old French force carried the noun into English in the thirteenth century with the senses of strength, violence and legal power.
items.cn: 古法语 force 在十三世纪把这个名词带入英语，带有力量、暴力与法律效力诸义。

items.en: By the medieval period force already covered armed bodies and the binding power of law, two branches that still run side by side.
items.cn: 到中世纪，force 已兼指武装队伍与法律的约束力，这两条分支至今并行。

items.en: Mechanics gave force its precise sense of a measurable push or pull, a use that became standard in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 力学赋予 force 可测量的推拉作用这一精确含义，这一用法在十七世纪成为标准。

items.en: The first dates for the physics sense and for the collective military sense are approximate; the noun itself is well attested from the medieval period.
items.cn: 物理义与集体军事义的最早记录年代为约数；这个名词本身在中世纪已有充分记录。

note.en: The first group either shares the Latin adjective for strong or merely looks like force; the second group separates force from neighbouring words for power and pressure.
note.cn: 第一组或共享那个表示「强壮」的拉丁形容词，或只是形似 force；第二组把 force 与相邻的「权力、压力」等词区分开。

entries.definition: From Latin fortis through French, but it names a stronghold, a place built to resist, not strength itself.
entries.definitionCN: 经法语来自拉丁 fortis，但指堡垒，即一座为抵抗而建的处所，不是力量本身。

entries.definition: From Italian forte 'strong', ultimately Latin fortis; it names a person's strong point, or a loud passage in music.
entries.definitionCN: 来自意大利语 forte「强壮」，最终出自拉丁 fortis；指一个人的长处，或音乐中响亮的段落。

entries.definition: A strengthened place, built on the same Latin adjective; it is a noun of place, not of power.
entries.definitionCN: 加固的城堡，由同一拉丁形容词构成；是表示地点的名词，不是力量。

entries.definition: From in- plus force: to put strength behind a rule so that it is obeyed.
entries.definitionCN: 由表「进入」的前缀加 force 构成：把力量放到规则背后，使其被遵守。

entries.definition: A smithy and the verb to shape metal; it comes from Latin fabrica 'workshop', not from fortis, so it only looks related.
entries.definitionCN: 指铁匠铺与锻打金属的动词；来自拉丁 fabrica「作坊」，而非 fortis，只是形似而已。

entries.definition: The quality of being strong in body or material; force can also mean the push itself.
entries.definitionCN: 身体或材料强健的性质；force 还能指推拉作用本身。

entries.definition: A broader word for ability or authority; force adds the idea of pressure applied.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指能力或权威的更宽说法；force 多一层「施加压力」的意思。

entries.definition: A steady push spread over a surface; force is the total push, pressure is that push divided by area.
entries.definitionCN: 分布在表面上的持续推力；force 是总推力，pressure 是单位面积上的推力。

entries.definition: Force used to injure or damage; it is the destructive edge of force.
entries.definitionCN: 用以伤害或破坏的力量；是 force 中带破坏性的那一面。

entries.definition: A verb for making someone act; force can do the same but also names the strength behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 使人行动的一个动词；force 也能这样用，但同时指背后的力量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Fortis is Latin for strong, and fortitude is the strength to endure.
normal.cn: fortis 是拉丁语「强壮」，fortitude 就是能坚持的力量。

normal.en: The family runs force, forced, forceful, enforce and reinforce.
normal.cn: 同族词有 force、forced、forceful、enforce 与 reinforce。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the main senses: come into force, labour force, air force, by force.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出主要义项：生效、劳动力、空军、强行地。

normal.en: Physics measures force in newtons, and every force has a direction.
normal.cn: 物理以牛顿为单位量力，每一个力都有方向。

normal.en: Law says a rule in force is one that can be enforced.
normal.cn: 法律说一条正在生效的规则，就是能被强制执行的那条。

abstract.en: Picture a bent beam slowly returning to a straight line under a jack.
abstract.cn: 想象一根弯梁在千斤顶下慢慢回到直线。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd leaning together against a gate until the hinges give way.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人一起压在门上，直到铰链撑不住。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing a stamp down hard enough to leave a mark.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手用力压下印章，留下清晰的痕迹。

examples.en: The engineers calculated the force needed to lift the span.
examples.cn: 工程师算出了抬起这跨梁所需的力。

examples.en: The old law is no longer in force.
examples.cn: 那条旧法律已不再生效。

examples.en: A strong wind forced the ferry to stay in port.
examples.cn: 大风迫使渡轮留在港内。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「for（为了）+ ce（策）」——为了推行一套策，就得使出力气；force 力量、武力、迫使

root: 拉丁 fortis「强壮」→ 晚期拉丁 fortia「力量」（复数）→ 古法语 force「力量、武力」→ 英语 force；物理「力」义自十七世纪力学，「部队」义由「兵力」的集体用法而来。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses grow from one strong hand: the hand pushes a body, shows its own strength, compels a person, backs a rule, moves a mind, gathers into a troop, is counted as manpower, and finally acts as a verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一只强壮的手长出：手推动物体、显出力气、强迫人、为规则撑腰、推动人心、聚成队伍、被计为人力，最后转为动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a strong hand that pushes until something yields.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只强壮的手一直推，直到某物让步。

branches.en: PUSH AND STRENGTH: a measurable push, and the plain strength a body or blow carries.
branches.cn: 推力与力气：可测量的推拉作用，以及身体或一击所带的直白力量。

branches.en: COMPULSION: the same push turned against a resisting person.
branches.cn: 强制：同一个推力转向一个抵抗的人。

branches.en: POWER BEHIND WORDS: a rule is enforced, an argument convinces, both by invisible pushing.
branches.cn: 言语背后的力量：规则被强制执行，论证说服人心，都是看不见的推力。

branches.en: STRENGTH IN NUMBERS: armed men and workers are gathered and counted as one force.
branches.cn: 人多成势：武装人员与工人被聚拢，计作一股力量。

branches.en: THE VERB: the hand that pushed becomes the act of forcing.
branches.cn: 动词：曾经推动的那只手，变成「迫使」这个动作。

intro.en: Force is a Latin noun of strength that became an English noun, verb and a whole family of derived words.
intro.cn: force 是一个表示力量的拉丁名词，在英语里成为名词、动词，并衍生出整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin fortis 'strong' gives fortia and force, and also fortitude, fort and fortress; the English prefix en- builds enforce from the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fortis「强壮」衍生 fortia 与 force，也衍生 fortitude、fort 与 fortress；英语前缀 en- 由同一词干构成 enforce。

items.example: The adjective supplies the strength behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词为整个词族提供「力量」的底子。

items.structure: late Latin plural noun from fortis
items.example: The late Latin plural is the form usually cited behind the French noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个晚期拉丁复数，一般认为就是法语名词背后的形式。

items.example: The jack applied a steady force.

items.structure: force plus plural or third-person ending
items.example: Enemy forces withdrew from the valley.
She gave a forced smile and left.
items.exampleCN: 她勉强笑了一下就走开了。

items.example: The chair gave a forceful reply.
He argued forcefully for the repair fund.
items.exampleCN: 他为维修基金展开了有力的论证。

items.meaning: to put force behind a rule
items.meaningCN: 把力量加在规则上；执行
items.example: Officers enforce the parking ban every morning.
items.exampleCN: 执法人员每天上午执行禁停规定。

items.example: Steel bars reinforce the concrete wall.
items.exampleCN: 钢筋加固了这面混凝土墙。

definition_zh: 困难的；艰难的；难对付的；不易相处的
definition_en: hard to do, understand, or deal with
core_image: 一座爬不上去的陡坡，每一步都要用力
scene: 数学考试最后一道题，全班只有一个人做出来。 The last question was too difficult for most of us, so we left it blank.
sceneCN: 这里 difficult 是「困难的」（第 1 个义项：难以完成）；句意是最后一题对我们大多数人来说太难，只好空着。

derivatives.zh: difficult 加名词后缀 -y 构成，义为「困难；难题」
difficult 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「困难地」

senses.title: Hard to do or understand
senses.definition: needing much effort or skill to do, understand, or answer
senses.definitionCN: 需要很大努力或技巧才能完成、理解或回答
senses.example: This puzzle is difficult, but I will not give up.
senses.exampleCN: 这道谜题很难，但我不会放弃。
senses.why: The Latin root ficultas carries the idea of effort and even trickery, so the word paints a task that pushes back against you.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根带有「费力」甚至「刁难」的意思，所以这个词描绘的是会「顶回来」的任务。

senses.title: Hard to deal with
senses.definition: not easy to get along with or to manage
senses.definitionCN: 不容易相处或应付
senses.example: My cousin can be difficult when he is hungry.
senses.exampleCN: 我表弟饿的时候挺难对付的。
senses.why: A person can push back just like a hard task, so the image of resistance moved from work to people.
senses.whyCN: 人会像难题一样「顶人」，抵抗的画面便从事情转移到了人身上。

senses.title: Full of trouble
senses.definition: full of problems or worry
senses.definitionCN: 充满问题或忧虑
senses.example: It was a difficult year for our family, but we stayed together.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年我们家过得很艰难，但我们一直在一起。
senses.why: When every step costs effort and the road stays steep, life itself is called difficult.
senses.whyCN: 当每一步都费劲、坡一直很陡时，生活本身也被称作 difficult。

intro.en: Difficult is built on Latin parts about effort and trickery.
intro.cn: difficult 由拉丁语中表示费力、刁难的成分构成。

items.en: The root dificultas came from difficilis, meaning not easy, built on dis- (not) and facilis (easy to do).
items.cn: 拉丁语 dificultas 出自 difficilis（不容易），由 dis-（不）加 facilis（容易做的）构成。

items.en: Facilis itself came from facere, to make or to do.
items.cn: facilis 又来自动词 facere（做、制作）。

items.en: Middle English borrowed difficult from Old French and Latin around the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 约在十五世纪，中古英语经古法语从拉丁语借入 difficult。

items.en: At first it often meant hard to please or stubborn about people.
items.cn: 最初它常指人难讨好、执拗。

items.en: Modern English keeps both the hard-task sense and the hard-person sense.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留「难事」和「难对付的人」两个义项。

note.en: These words share the hard-task field or the sound of difficult.
note.cn: 这些词属于难事义场，或与 difficult 读音相近。

entries.definition: noun: the state of being hard
entries.definitionCN: 名词：困难

entries.definition: not the same, different root
entries.definitionCN: 不同的（拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definitionCN: 能力（同出拉丁语 facere）

entries.definition: ease of doing, or a building

entries.definition: shy, different root
entries.definitionCN: 羞怯的（拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: needing effort

entries.definition: hard to do or endure
entries.definitionCN: 艰难的；坚韧的

entries.definition: full of traps or skill needed
entries.definitionCN: 棘手的

entries.definition: asking much effort
entries.definitionCN: 要求高的

entries.definition: not hard at all
entries.definitionCN: 容易的（反义）

normalIntro.en: Break the word into dis- and fic to see the not-easy core.
normalIntro.cn: 把 difficult 拆成 dis- 和 fic，看出「不容易」的核心。

normal.en: difficult = dis (not) + ficult (easy to do), so not easy.
normal.cn: difficult = dis（不）+ ficult（容易做），即「不容易」。

normal.en: difficulty is the noun: without difficulty means easily.
normal.cn: difficulty 是名词，without difficulty 意思是轻松地。

normal.en: facility is its cousin: easy doing.
normal.cn: facility 是它的近亲，意为「容易」。

normal.en: A difficult person is hard to get along with.
normal.cn: difficult person 指难相处的人。

normal.en: Say the question is difficult, not the paper is difficult.
normal.cn: 说题目 difficult，不说卷子本身 difficult。

abstract.en: Picture a steep hill where every step slips back a little.
abstract.cn: 想象一座陡坡，每迈一步都往回滑一点。

abstract.en: Feel your pencil stop on the last maths question.
abstract.cn: 体会铅笔停在最后一道数学题上的感觉。

abstract.en: Hear someone say this is going to be hard before a big match.
abstract.cn: 想象大赛前有人说这可不好办。

examples.en: English spelling is difficult, but practice makes it better.
examples.cn: 英语拼写很难，但多练就会变好。

examples.en: It is difficult for me to get up early in winter.
examples.cn: 冬天早起对我来说很困难。

examples.en: Grandpa had a difficult time after the storm, but neighbours helped him.
examples.cn: 暴风雨后爷爷的日子很难过，但邻居们帮了他。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「第非靠他」——第一反应「非靠他不可」，说明这事自己做不来，真难

root: 来自拉丁语 difficilis（不容易），dis-（不）+ facilis（容易做的）；facilis 出自动词 facere（做）。

sensesIntro.en: Difficult starts with hard tasks, then hard people and hard times.
sensesIntro.cn: difficult 先指难做的事，再指难对付的人和艰难的处境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steep slope that pushes back
core.cn: 核心意象：一座顶回来的陡坡

branches.en: A task needing great effort
branches.cn: 需要大力气的任务

branches.cn: 不好应付的人

branches.cn: 充满麻烦的时期

branches.cn: 从难走的一步到难熬的一年

branches.en: Resistance moving from work to people
branches.cn: 抵抗从事情转移到人身上

intro.cn: difficult 的拉丁前缀和后缀都写在脸上。

latinIntro.cn: 词族的核心是拉丁语 facere（做）。

definition_zh: 庆祝；庆典；庆祝活动
definition_en: a joyful event or party held to mark a special day or success
core_image: 彩带、气球与笑声装满整间教室
scene: 毕业典礼结束，操场上立刻变成了欢乐的海洋。 After the graduation ceremony the playground turned into one big celebration.
sceneCN: 这里 celebration 是「庆祝活动」（第 1 个义项：纪念好事的欢乐聚会）；句意为毕业典礼后操场成了欢乐海洋。

derivatives.zh: 其动词原形，义为「庆祝」
同根词，义为「名人」

senses.title: A joyful event for a special day
senses.definition: a party or event held to mark something happy
senses.definitionCN: 为纪念喜事而举行的聚会或活动
senses.example: The wedding celebration lasted till midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 婚庆一直持续到午夜。
senses.why: The Latin celebrare meant honouring in company, and a company-honouring became an event.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 celebrare 意为聚众礼赞，聚众之举便成了一场活动。

senses.title: The act of celebrating
senses.definition: the action of marking a happy occasion
senses.definitionCN: 纪念喜事的行为本身
senses.example: The celebration of the win began in the locker room.
senses.exampleCN: 对胜利的庆祝从更衣室就开始了。
senses.why: The -ion ending turns the verb's deed into a nameable act.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ion 把动词的行为变成可命名之事。

intro.en: Celebration is celebrate wearing its Latin action ending.
intro.cn: celebration 就是 celebrate 戴上拉丁动作后缀。

items.en: Latin celebrare meant to honour and perform publicly.
items.cn: 拉丁语 celebrare 意为公开礼赞与举行。

items.en: Late Latin celebratio named the act of honouring.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 celebratio 指礼赞之行。

items.en: Old French celebration passed the act-name onward.
items.cn: 古法语 celebration 把行为之名传了下去。

items.en: Middle English celebration first meant religious rites.
items.cn: 中古英语 celebration 起初指宗教仪式。

items.en: Modern English generalised it to every joyful event.
items.cn: 现代英语将其泛化为一切欢庆活动。

note.en: The first group collects family words; the second collects festive-event words.
note.cn: 第一组收词族词，第二组收节庆活动类词。

entries.definition: The verb behind this noun.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「庆祝」，是本词的动词原形。

entries.definition: A famous person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「名人」，同根。

entries.definition: Movement around, as of blood or news.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「循环；流传」，尾形相同而词源不同。

entries.definition: A social event with fun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「聚会」，规模更随意。

entries.definition: A public day of joy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「节日」，更公开定期。

entries.definition: A formal event with set steps.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「典礼」，更庄重。

normalIntro.en: Remember celebration as celebrate plus ion.
normalIntro.cn: celebration 就是 celebrate 加 ion。

normal.en: celebrate + ion = celebration, the act made a thing.
normal.cn: celebrate 加 ion，动作变成事件。

normal.en: in celebration of means for the joy of.
normal.cn: in celebration of 即「为庆祝…」。

normal.en: celebrations often mean balloons and songs.
normal.cn: celebrations 总少不了气球与歌声。

normal.en: a celebrity is a much-celebrated person.
normal.cn: celebrity 是被频频庆祝的人。

normal.en: class celebrations follow every exam week.
normal.cn: 考试周后必有班级庆祝。

abstract.en: Smell the cake, hear the pop of balloons.
abstract.cn: 闻蛋糕的甜香，听气球炸响。

abstract.en: See the long table crowded with smiling faces.
abstract.cn: 长桌边挤满笑脸。

abstract.en: Feel a paper hat too big sliding over one ear.
abstract.cn: 纸帽太大，滑过一只耳朵。

examples.en: The school held a celebration for its ninetieth birthday.
examples.cn: 学校为九十周年校庆举办了庆典。

examples.en: Every goal was followed by wild celebration.
examples.cn: 每次进球后都有一阵狂喜庆祝。

examples.en: They wore red shirts in celebration of the New Year.
examples.cn: 他们穿上红衫庆祝新年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赛了雷身」——赢赛那天雷声般的欢呼洒满全身。

root: 拉丁语 celebris（著名的）→ celebrare（礼赞）→ celebratio（礼赞之行）→ 古法语 celebration → 英语 celebration；同族 celebrate、celebrity。

sensesIntro.en: Celebration names both the joyful event and the act of honouring it.
sensesIntro.cn: celebration 既命名欢乐的活动，也命名礼赞的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room filled on purpose with joy
core.cn: 核心意象：一间被人特意装满欢乐的屋子

branches.en: Parties and public feasts
branches.cn: 聚会与公共盛宴

branches.en: The doing of the honouring
branches.cn: 礼赞行为本身

branches.en: Birthdays, wins and New Years
branches.cn: 生日、胜利与新年

branches.en: Music, food and decorations
branches.cn: 音乐、美食与布置

branches.en: Joy arranged to be remembered
branches.cn: 被安排得值得铭记的欢乐

intro.en: Celebration shows how -ion freezes a verb into an event.
intro.cn: celebration 展示 -ion 如何把动词凝固成一场事件。

latinIntro.en: From celebrare Latin built celebratio, its act-noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语由 celebrare 造出行为名词 celebratio。

definition_zh: 扔；投掷；抛；（使）陷入（某种状态）；举办
definition_en: to send something through the air with your hand, or to cause someone to be in a particular state
core_image: 手臂向后一拉，手腕一甩，东西划出一道弧线飞出去
scene: 院子里父子俩来回扔着球,球在阳光下划出一道又一道弧线。 The father threw the ball high and the boy ran to catch it.
sceneCN: 这里 throw 是「扔、抛」（第 1 个义项：用手把东西投向空中）；句意为父亲把球高高扔起，男孩跑过去接住。

pos.zh: 使陷入（某种状态）；使困惑
举办（聚会）；投射（光线、影子）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -er 构成，义为「投掷者；（机器）抛掷装置」
由 throw 与 away 复合，义为「用完即弃的；随口说出的话」
由 throw 与 back 复合，义为「复古之物；返祖现象」

senses.title: To send something through the air
senses.definition: to send something through the air with your hand, using a quick movement of the arm
senses.definitionCN: 用手臂快速动作把东西送向空中
senses.example: He threw the keys across the table to me.
senses.exampleCN: 他把钥匙隔着桌子扔给我。
senses.why: The root meant to twist or turn, and the arm turns as it hurls something away.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「扭、转」，手臂在甩出东西时正是扭转的。

senses.title: To make someone be in a state
senses.definition: to cause someone or something to be suddenly in a particular state or situation
senses.definitionCN: 使人或事物突然进入某种状态或处境
senses.example: The news threw the whole office into confusion.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息让整个办公室陷入混乱。
senses.why: A blow of feeling hurls a mind the way a hand hurls a stone.
senses.whyCN: 情绪的打击把心甩出去，就像手甩出一块石头。

senses.title: To shine or cast light and shadow
senses.definition: to send light or shadow onto a surface
senses.definitionCN: 把光或影投到某表面上
senses.example: The low sun threw long shadows across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 低斜的太阳在田野上投下长长的影子。
senses.why: Light and shadow are thrown like objects: they travel from the source and land on a surface.
senses.whyCN: 光与影像物体一样被抛出：从源头飞出，落在表面上。

senses.title: To hold a party or event
senses.definition: to organise and hold a party, dinner or similar social event
senses.definitionCN: 组织和举办聚会、晚宴等社交活动
senses.example: They threw a party for her return.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为她的归来办了一场聚会。
senses.why: A party is launched the way an object is thrown: set in motion and let go.
senses.whyCN: 聚会像物体一样被抛出：先使它动起来，再松手放手。

senses.title: To be pushed off a horse or in a fight
senses.definition: to make a rider fall from a horse, or to make someone fall in a fight
senses.definitionCN: 使骑手从马上摔下，或在搏斗中把对方摔倒
senses.example: The horse threw its rider at the first fence.
senses.exampleCN: 那匹马在第一道栅栏处把骑手摔了下来。
senses.why: The rider is thrown off, the same physical hurl applied to a person.
senses.whyCN: 骑手被甩了下来，还是那同一次物理的投掷，只是对象换成了人。

intro.en: Throw is a native English verb from a root meaning to twist or turn, the same family as thread.
intro.cn: throw 是英语本土动词，源自意为「扭、转」的词根，与 thread 同族。

items.en: The root meant to twist or turn round, which describes the motion of an arm hurling something.
items.cn: 词根意为「扭、转」，正描述手臂甩出东西的动作。

items.en: Old English þrāwan meant to twist or turn, and only later took on the sense of hurling through the air.
items.cn: 古英语 þrāwan 意为「扭、转」，后来才获得「抛向空中」之义。

items.en: Middle English throw covered casting, hurling and even throwing a rider, and the noun throw appeared beside it.
items.cn: 中古英语 throw 兼指投、掷，乃至把骑手摔下，旁生名词 throw。

items.en: Modern English added abstract and social uses: to throw light on a question, to throw a party.
items.cn: 现代英语增添了抽象与社交用法：throw light on a question、throw a party。

items.en: The phrasal patterns, throw away and throw up, gave the verb a large second life in everyday speech.
items.cn: throw away 与 throw up 这类短语搭配，让这个动词在日常口语中获得了极大的第二生命。

note.en: The first group gathers the throwing family and near spellings; the second compares verbs of sending things outward.
note.cn: 第一组收投掷词族与形近词；第二组比较表示「送出」的动词。

entries.definition: The past tense, sounding like through but meaning threw.
entries.definitionCN: 过去式；读音与 through 相同

entries.definition: The past participle, used after have or be.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词

entries.definition: A person or machine that throws.
entries.definitionCN: 投掷者；抛掷装置

entries.definition: From one side to the other; the same sound as threw.
entries.definitionCN: 穿过；与 threw 同音

entries.definition: To throw lightly or carelessly, often upward.
entries.definitionCN: 轻抛；随手扔（常向上）

entries.definition: To throw with great force, often in anger.
entries.definitionCN: 猛掷（带力量与怒气）

entries.definition: To throw with a sudden, wild movement.
entries.definitionCN: 猛甩；乱扔

entries.definition: To throw or send out, especially light, a shadow or a vote.
entries.definitionCN: 投；投射（正式，常用于光、影、票）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the twisting root, the irregular forms and the phrasal uses.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自「扭、转」词根、不规则变化，以及短语搭配。

normal.en: Throw, threw, thrown: the vowel shifts from -ow to -ew to -own, like grow and blow.
normal.cn: throw, threw, thrown：元音从 -ow 变 -ew 再到 -own，与 grow、blow 相同。

normal.en: Thrown is the past participle; threw is only for the simple past.
normal.cn: thrown 是过去分词；threw 只用于一般过去时。

normal.en: The root meant to twist, and your arm twists as it throws.
normal.cn: 词根意为「扭」，手臂在扔出时正是扭转的。

normal.en: Throw light on means to make a problem clear, as if light were thrown at it.
normal.cn: throw light on 意为让问题变清楚，就像把光投在上面。

normal.en: Throw a party does not mean throwing anything away: it means holding one.
normal.cn: throw a party 不是把聚会扔掉，而是举办聚会。

abstract.en: Picture a stone leaving the hand in a curve, the arm still turning behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象石头以弧线离手，手臂还在身后转动。

abstract.en: The verb sends not just objects but light, shadows and states of mind.
abstract.cn: 这个动词送出的不只是物体，还有光、影与心境。

abstract.en: Everything thrown is briefly free of the hand that held it.
abstract.cn: 被抛出的一切，都短暂地离开了托着它的手。

examples.en: She threw the ball back over the fence.
examples.cn: 她把球扔回栅栏那边。

examples.en: The report throws new light on the accident.
examples.cn: 这份报告让事故有了新的解释。

examples.en: They threw a party when the project was finished.
examples.cn: 项目完成后他们办了一场聚会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「思入」——把思虑一股脑扔进风里 → throw 扔

root: 古英语 þrāwan，源自日耳曼词根「扭、转」（与 thread 同族），本义「扭转」，后转指以扭转的手臂抛掷；由物理投掷引申出投射光影子、使人陷入状态、举办活动等义。

sensesIntro.en: Throw begins as an arm twisting something into the air and then throws light, shadows, states of mind and even parties.
sensesIntro.cn: throw 起初是手臂一扭把东西甩向空中，后来也抛出光、影、心境，乃至一场聚会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone leaving the hand in a curve, the arm still turning.
core.cn: 核心意象：石头以弧线离手，手臂仍在转动。

branches.en: The object: keys, a ball, a stone.
branches.cn: 物体线：钥匙、球、石头。

branches.en: The abstract throw: feelings and shadows flung outward.
branches.cn: 抽象线：情绪与影子被甩出去。

branches.en: The social throw: a party organised and launched.
branches.cn: 社交线：聚会从筹办到开启。

branches.en: The violent throw: a rider off a horse.
branches.cn: 暴力线：骑手被摔下马。

branches.en: Hand and emotion share one hurling verb.
branches.cn: 手与情绪共用同一个「甩」的动词。

intro.en: Throw takes -er for the doer, and it compounds with away and back.
intro.cn: throw 加 -er 表施事者，并与 away、back 构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词为日耳曼本土词，拉丁词条留空。

items.meaning: a return to an older type

items.example: Project the image on the wall.

definition_zh: 永远；永久；老是，不停地
definition_en: for all time in the future; again and again or constantly
core_image: 一条没有尽头的直线：时间一直往前延伸，停不下来
scene: 毕业典礼上，两位好朋友把名字刻在校门口的老树上，约定这份友情不会消失。 They promised that their friendship would last forever.
sceneCN: 这里 forever 是「永远」的意思（第 1 个义项：时间上无限延续）；两个朋友把友情比作刻在树上的名字，认为它会一直延续下去。

pos.zh: 老是；不停地（常与进行时连用）

derivatives.zh: forever 的形容词化表达，义为「永恒的；永久的」
与 forever 同义的形容词，义为「永久的；不朽的」
eternal 的名词形式，义为「永恒；来世」

senses.title: For all future time
senses.definition: for all time in the future, without ending
senses.definitionCN: 在未来的所有时间里持续下去，没有终点。
senses.example: I will remember this trip forever.
senses.exampleCN: 我会永远记住这次旅行。
senses.why: The word joins for (during) with ever (always), so the core image is time stretching without an end.
senses.whyCN: forever 由 for（在……期间）加 ever（总是）构成，核心意象是时间被拉长、看不到尽头。

senses.title: Again and again; constantly
senses.definition: used to say that someone does something very often, often annoyingly
senses.definitionCN: 表示某人经常做某事，常带抱怨或调侃语气。
senses.example: My little brother is forever borrowing my phone.
senses.exampleCN: 我弟弟老是借我的手机。
senses.why: In modern spoken English, the idea of endless time was applied to endless repetition, so forever also means doing something all the time.
senses.whyCN: 现代口语把「时间没有尽头」引申到「动作反复不停」，于是 forever 又有了「老是、总在」的用法。

senses.title: For a very long time (hyperbole)
senses.definition: used for emphasizing that something takes a very long time
senses.definitionCN: 用于夸张地强调某事耗时极长，并非真的永远。
senses.example: The queue at the canteen took forever today.
senses.exampleCN: 今天食堂的队排得久死了。
senses.why: Because forever is the longest possible time, speakers stretch it hyperbolically to any long wait.
senses.whyCN: 因为 forever 是最长的时间单位，说话人用夸张手法把任何漫长的等待都说成 forever。

intro.en: Forever is a transparent English compound, first recorded in the Middle English period, built from two native words.
intro.cn: forever 是一个结构透明的英语复合词，首见于中古英语时期，由两个本土词拼接而成。

items.en: The first element, fore, meant 'before, in front of' and the second, æfre (later ever), meant 'always, at any time'.
items.cn: 第一个成分 fore 意为「在前、在先」，第二个成分 æfre（后来写作 ever）意为「总是、任何时候」。

items.en: The two words fused into the compound phrase 'for ever', recorded around the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 两个词在十三世纪前后融合成复合短语 for ever，见于中古英语文献。

items.en: The phrase was later written as one word 'forever', which is now the standard American spelling and common everywhere.
items.cn: 这个短语后来合并拼写为 forever，如今是标准的美式拼法，各地通用。

items.en: The repetitive sense 'constantly' developed in colloquial use, especially in British English with continuous tenses.
items.cn: 「不停地」这一义项在口语中发展出来，英国英语尤其常与进行时连用。

items.en: Hyperbolic uses like 'take forever' spread in everyday speech to describe long waits.
items.cn: take forever 之类的夸张用法在日常口语里流行开来，用来形容漫长等待。

note.en: Words near forever and words that also express endless time or endless repetition.
note.cn: 与 forever 形近或同样表达无限时间、无休止重复的词。

entries.definition: toward the front or ahead in time; similar spelling with the same for- beginning
entries.definitionCN: 向前或提前；与 forever 拼写相近、同样以 for- 开头，但意思完全不同。

entries.definition: to lose a right or prize as a penalty; begins with for- but is unrelated
entries.definitionCN: 因受罚而丧失权利或奖赏；以 for- 开头，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: to search widely for food or supplies; shares letters with forever by chance
entries.definitionCN: 四处搜寻食物或物资；与 forever 字母相近纯属巧合。

entries.definition: at all times; overlaps with the repetition sense of forever
entries.definitionCN: 总是；始终；与 forever 的「不停地」义项重叠。

entries.definition: for all time, in a formal or literary tone
entries.definitionCN: 永久地；语气正式、书面，与 forever 的「永远」义项相近。

entries.definition: continuously, without stopping
entries.definitionCN: 持续不断地；与 forever 的「老是」义项相近，语气较正式。

normalIntro.en: Five memory hooks based on the parts and everyday phrases of forever.
normalIntro.cn: 基于 forever 的构词成分和常用搭配的五条记忆钩子。

normal.en: Split forever into for + ever: 'during ever' means during all time.
normal.cn: 把 forever 拆成 for + ever：「在这段所有时间里」，自然就是永远。

normal.en: for- here is not the 'for the sake of' preposition but the old 'forward in time' element.
normal.cn: 这里的 for- 不是介词「为了」，而是古义「往前推时间」的成分。

normal.en: Remember the phrase 'last forever' with an old oak tree that outlives generations.
normal.cn: 记住搭配 last forever，联想一棵比几代人活得都久的古橡树。

normal.en: 'Take forever' is what a slow queue feels like: the wait has no end.
normal.cn: take forever 形容慢吞吞的排队：等待仿佛没有尽头。

normal.en: British style: 'He is forever losing keys' — forever before an -ing verb means again and again.
normal.cn: 英式用法：forever 放在动词进行时前表示「老是」，如 He is forever losing keys。

abstract.en: Picture a straight line with no right end drawn across the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一条画满整页纸、右端没有终点的直线。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose hands never move because time itself stopped.
abstract.cn: 想象一个指针永远不动的钟，时间本身停住了。

abstract.en: Picture a song repeating on loop that you cannot switch off.
abstract.cn: 想象一首单曲循环、怎么也关不掉的歌。

examples.en: Nothing lasts forever, so enjoy the good days while they are here.
examples.cn: 没有什么是永恒的，所以在好日子还在时好好享受。

examples.en: The download is taking forever; I have been waiting for half an hour.
examples.cn: 下载慢得要命，我已经等了半个小时。

examples.en: She is forever reminding me to water the plants.
examples.cn: 她老是提醒我给植物浇水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拂藕」——轻轻拂开藕的丝，丝断丝连永远扯不完，就像 forever 的时间没有尽头。

root: forever 是本土复合词：for（古英语，指「向前推进的时间」）+ ever（古英语 æfre，指「总是、任何时候」）。字面即「在所有时间里」，引申为「永远」；口语中又把无限时间投射到无限重复的动作上，产生「老是」义。

sensesIntro.en: Forever moves from endless time to endless repetition to exaggerated long waits.
sensesIntro.cn: forever 从「无限的时间」走向「无休止的重复」，再走向夸张化的「漫长的等待」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: time stretched into a line that never ends
core.cn: 核心意象：时间被拉成一条没有尽头的直线

branches.en: A promise or state that continues through all time
branches.cn: 承诺或状态贯穿所有时间，永远持续

branches.en: Endless time mapped onto endless repetition of an action
branches.cn: 无限时间投射到动作的无休止重复上

branches.en: A habit complained about in the continuous tense
branches.cn: 用进行时抱怨某人的习惯性动作

branches.en: The longest time used as a ruler for any long wait
branches.cn: 把最长时间概念当作量尺，夸张地形容漫长等待

branches.en: Hyperbole turns eternity into everyday complaint
branches.cn: 夸张手法把「永恒」降格为日常抱怨用语

intro.en: Forever is a compound of two everyday English words, so its parts are easy to see.
intro.cn: forever 由两个日常英语词合成，成分一目了然。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root inside forever; related English compounds use the same native elements.
latinIntro.cn: forever 内部没有拉丁词根；英语中用同样本土成分构成的复合词可作参照。

items.meaningCN: 在时间上向前；持续期间
items.example: A forerunner runs ahead of the others.
items.exampleCN: forerunner 指「先行者」，for- 表示「在前」。

items.example: Ever since that day, we write to each other.
items.exampleCN: ever since 表示「自那以后一直」。

items.example: She never eats breakfast before noon.

items.exampleCN: everywhere 把「每个」加到「地点」上。

items.example: Everything in the fridge is fresh.
However hard it rained, we kept walking.
The hills seemed everlasting to the child.
items.exampleCN: everlasting 是 forever 的形容词化。
evergreen 由「总是」加「绿色」构成。

definition_zh: 练习；执业；奉行；施展（手法）
definition_en: the British spelling of the verb meaning to do something repeatedly in order to improve, to work as a doctor or lawyer, to follow a religion or custom, or to perform a trick
core_image: 一个人对着镜子把同一句台词念到嘴唇自己会动，镜面上全是呼出的白雾
scene: 剧场后台只剩一盏化妆灯，演员对着镜子把同一句台词又念了一遍，声音沙哑却没有停。 She practises the line until it sounds like a thought rather than a recitation.
sceneCN: 这里 practise 是「练习」（第 1 个义项：为熟练而反复做某事）；句意为她反复练那句台词，直到它听起来像临时想到的，而不是背出来的。画面里有化妆灯、镜子和沙哑的嗓音。

pos.zh: 练习；执业；奉行；施展（手法）

derivatives.zh: 由 practise 的过去分词转作形容词，义为「熟练的；老练的」
由 practise 的现在分词转作形容词，义为「执业中的；正在从事某职业的」
英式英语中与动词 practise 分工的名词形式，义为「练习；实践；诊所」
由 practise 的词干加表示从业者的后缀构成，义为「从业者」

senses.title: To do something repeatedly in order to improve
senses.definition: to do an activity many times so that your skill at it improves
senses.definitionCN: 反复进行某项活动，使自己的技能有所提高
senses.example: She practises the violin for an hour before breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 她早饭前练一个小时小提琴。
senses.why: The Greek source meant to do, so the verb starts from the plain act of doing a thing over and over rather than from thinking about it.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语来源意为「做」，所以这个动词的起点就是把一件事一遍遍做下去，而不是在脑子里琢磨。

senses.title: To work in a profession
senses.definition: to work as a doctor, lawyer or other trained professional
senses.definitionCN: 以医生、律师或其他受过训练的专业人士身份工作
senses.example: He has practised law in this city for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在这个城市当了二十年律师。
senses.why: Professional work is skill applied daily, so the verb that means repeating an action also names the lifelong carrying out of a trained job.
senses.whyCN: 专业工作就是每天把本领用出来，所以表示反复练习的动词，也用来指把受训得来的职业做一辈子。

senses.title: To follow a religion or custom
senses.definition: to observe the rules and ceremonies of a religion or a traditional custom
senses.definitionCN: 遵守某种宗教或传统习俗的规矩与仪式
senses.example: Her family still practises the old harvest festival.
senses.exampleCN: 她家仍然遵行古老的丰收节习俗。
senses.why: A custom survives only by being done again each year, and the verb for repeated doing fits that annual repetition exactly.
senses.whyCN: 习俗只有年年重新做一遍才能延续，而表示反复去做的动词，正好贴合这种一年一度的重复。

senses.title: To carry out a trick or method
senses.definition: to perform a trick or use a method, especially one that is repeated on new victims
senses.definitionCN: 施展某种手法或使用某种办法，尤指把同一套把戏用在新的对象身上
senses.example: The swindler practised the same trick on three families.
senses.exampleCN: 那个骗子把同一套把戏用在了三户人家身上。
senses.why: If the core is doing something again and again, the word can also describe a trick worked repeatedly on whoever comes next.
senses.whyCN: 既然核心是一遍遍去做，这个词也就能描述一套把戏，反复用在下一个上钩的人身上。

intro.en: Practise shares its whole history with practice, but English sends the verb down the -ise path and keeps -ice for the noun.
intro.cn: practise 与 practice 共享全部历史，只是英语让动词走 -ise 一路，把 -ice 留给名词。

items.en: The verb prassein, Attic prattein, meant to do or to achieve, and the whole family grows from the idea of action.
items.cn: 动词 prassein（阿提卡方言 prattein）意为做、完成，整个词族都从这个「行动」的念头长出来。

items.en: Praktikos described what is fit for action, a word about real work rather than abstract knowledge.
items.cn: praktikos 形容适合行动的，说的是实际动手，而不是抽象知识。

items.en: Latin practicus and the medieval verb practicare named practical action, and the noun practica named the knowledge gained by doing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 practicus 与中世纪动词 practicare 指实际去做，名词 practica 则指通过实践得来的知识。

items.en: Old French practiser, also written pratiquer, meant to put into practice or to carry on a profession, and English took the verb form from it.
items.cn: 古法语 practiser（也写作 pratiquer）意为付诸实践或从事某职业，英语的动词形式就是从它借来的。

items.en: Middle English practisen settled into practise, and British English now keeps practise for the verb while American English uses practice for both; the split is a spelling convention, not a difference in meaning.
items.cn: 中古英语 practisen 定型为 practise，如今英式英语用 practise 作动词、practice 作名词，美式英语两者都写 practice；这一分工只是拼写惯例，并不带来含义差别。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noun twin and the Latin-derived family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for training, drilling and carrying something out.
note.cn: 形近组收与它配对的名词形式以及拉丁来源的词族；近义组收表示训练、操练与执行的动词。

entries.definition: The noun in British English, and both noun and verb in American English.
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语中的名词，在美式英语中则名词动词同形。

entries.definition: Useful and concerned with real action rather than theory.
entries.definitionCN: 有用的、关乎实际行动而非理论的。

entries.definition: A person who practises a profession such as medicine or law.
entries.definitionCN: 从事医学、法律等职业的从业者。

entries.definition: A period of supervised practical training for students.
entries.definitionCN: 学生接受督导的实践训练期。

entries.definition: To practise a performance before showing it to an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 在观众面前演出之前进行排练。

entries.definition: To teach and exercise someone over time for a skill or a job.
entries.definitionCN: 用一段时间教导并训练某人掌握技能或胜任工作。

entries.definition: To make someone repeat an exercise until it becomes automatic.
entries.definitionCN: 让人反复做同一练习直到变成自动反应。

entries.definition: To perform a plan, order or method in real life.
entries.definitionCN: 在现实中执行计划、命令或方法。

normalIntro.en: The verb keeps the Greek sense of doing, the Latin layer of practical action, and a British spelling rule that separates it from the noun.
normalIntro.cn: 这个动词保留了希腊语「做」的意思与拉丁语「实际行动」这一层，再加一条把它跟名词分开的英式拼写规则。

normal.en: Practise uses -ise because British English marks verbs with that ending, as in realise and organise.
normal.cn: practise 用 -ise，是因为英式英语用这个词尾标记动词，就像 realise 与 organise。

normal.en: Practice uses -ice because it is the noun, just as advice is the noun beside the verb advise.
normal.cn: practice 用 -ice，因为它是名词，就像 advice 是名词、advise 是动词一样。

normal.en: American English uses practice for the verb too, so only British texts insist on the s.
normal.cn: 美式英语的动词也写 practice，所以只有英式文本才坚持用 s。

normal.en: The -ed form practised keeps the s and doubles nothing: practise, practised, practising.
normal.cn: 加 -ed 的过去式 practised 保留 s，也不双写任何字母：practise、practised、practising。

normal.en: Practise what you preach is the idiom that shows the plainest sense: do the thing, do not just talk about it.
normal.cn: practise what you preach 这个说法体现了最朴素的一层：真去做，而不只是嘴上讲。

abstract.en: A mirror in a cold dressing room is where skill is built: the same line, the same breath, again.
abstract.cn: 冷清的化妆间里那面镜子，就是本领被磨出来的地方：同一句词、同一口气，再来一遍。

abstract.en: A licence on the wall means nothing until the lawyer practises daily in front of real clients.
abstract.cn: 墙上的执照本身不算什么，直到律师每天在真实的当事人面前执业。

abstract.en: A custom lives only while someone practises it, which is why the verb also means to keep a tradition going.
abstract.cn: 习俗只有在有人继续照做时才活着，所以这个动词也意味着把传统延续下去。

examples.en: She practises the violin for an hour before breakfast.
examples.cn: 她早饭前练一个小时小提琴。

examples.en: He has practised law in this city for twenty years.
examples.cn: 他在这个城市当了二十年律师。

examples.en: The swindler practised the same trick on three families.
examples.cn: 那个骗子把同一套把戏用在了三户人家身上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来个试」——一个接一个的试验扑过来，练的就是手上功夫；记住 practise 是练习。

root: 与 practice 同源：希腊语 prassein/prattein（做）→ praktikos（适于行动的）→ 拉丁语 practicus → 中世纪拉丁语 practica/practicare → 古法语 practiser → 中古英语 practisen。英式英语中动词固定写作 practise、名词写作 practice；美式英语动词与名词都写 practice。

sensesIntro.en: The core is doing a thing over and over; the senses run from training a skill, to living by a profession, to keeping a custom, to working a trick on new victims.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把一件事反复做下去；义项从磨练技能，延伸到以某职业为生、遵行某种习俗，再到把一套把戏用在新的对象身上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a performer repeating one line at a mirror until the words come without effort.
core.cn: 核心意象：演员对着镜子重复同一句台词，直到字句毫不费力地出来。

branches.en: a mirror, a lamp and one line said thirty times
branches.cn: 一面镜子、一盏灯和一句念了三十遍的台词

branches.en: a brass plate on a solicitor's door
branches.cn: 律师门上一块黄铜名牌

branches.en: a family bowing at the same hour each week
branches.cn: 一家人每周同一时刻躬身

branches.en: the same trick played on a third stranger
branches.cn: 同一个把戏用在第三个陌生人身上

branches.en: hours of drill turning into a licence to work
branches.cn: 长时间操练换来一张执业许可

intro.en: A Greek verb of doing, a Latin verb of practical action, and the English verb ending -ise hold this spelling together.
intro.cn: 一个表示「做」的希腊动词、一个表示实际施行的拉丁动词，以及英语的动词词尾 -ise，共同撑起了这个拼写。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the adjective practicus and the medieval verb practicare, both built on the idea of practical action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了形容词 practicus 与中世纪动词 practicare，两者都建立在「实际去做」这一念头上。

items.meaning: to do repeatedly, to work in a profession

definition_zh: （will 的过去式）将、会；（表意愿）愿意、肯；（表推测）大概会；（表虚拟）就会、本来会；（表习惯）过去常常；（请求）请……好吗
definition_en: the past form of will, used for the future seen from the past, for polite requests, and for unreal situations
core_image: 一个人站在岔路口，看着那条没走的路
scene: 朋友邀你吃饭，你已经在忙，只回了一句下次一定。 When I was young, we would walk to school together.
sceneCN: 这里 would 表示「过去常常」（第 5 个义项：过去的反复习惯）；句意为小时候我们常常一起走路上学。看着那条没走的路，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 情态动词：将、会；愿意；大概会；就会（虚拟）；过去常常；（礼貌请求）

derivatives.zh: 情态动词，义为「将、会」，是 would 的原形
缩合形式，义为「不会」，是 would not 的口语形
形容词，义为「愿意的」，与 would 同源于「意愿」
名词，义为「意志」，同源名词
形容词，义为「未来的、自称的」，由 would 加 be 合成

senses.title: Future seen from the past
senses.titleCN: 过去的将来：从过去看那一刻的将然
senses.definition: the past form of will, for a future viewed from a past moment
senses.definitionCN: will 的过去式，表示从过去某点看将来
senses.example: He said he would come back before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 他说他天黑前会回来。
senses.why: English pushes will one step back in time; the reported future keeps its shape but takes the past form.
senses.whyCN: 英语把 will 向后推一步；被转述的将来形状不变，只是领了过去的形态。

senses.title: Willingness
senses.definition: used to express willingness or refusal
senses.definitionCN: 用来表示愿意或拒绝
senses.example: She would not listen to any excuse.
senses.exampleCN: 她什么借口都不肯听。
senses.why: The original will in English meant to want; that wanting survives in would you and I would gladly.
senses.whyCN: will 在英语里原意是「想要」，这层「想要」留在 would you 与 I would gladly 里。

senses.title: Polite requests
senses.titleCN: 礼貌请求：把话说得软一些
senses.definition: used to make a request less direct and more polite
senses.definitionCN: 用来使请求不那么直接、更客气
senses.example: Would you close the window, please?
senses.exampleCN: 请你把窗户关上好吗？
senses.why: Distance in grammar is politeness: the past form stands further from the listener than will.
senses.whyCN: 语法上的距离就是礼貌：过去式比 will 离听话人更远一步。

senses.title: Unreal conditions
senses.titleCN: 虚拟：与事实相反的情形
senses.definition: used in the result clause of an unreal condition
senses.definitionCN: 用在虚拟条件的结果分句里
senses.example: If I had known, I would have called you.
senses.exampleCN: 要是我当时知道，就会给你打电话了。
senses.why: A form that is one step back from reality is perfect for describing what did not happen.
senses.whyCN: 比现实退后一步的形式，正好用来描述没有发生的事。

senses.title: Past habit
senses.titleCN: 过去常常：反复发生的旧习惯
senses.definition: used for repeated actions in the past
senses.definitionCN: 用来表示过去反复发生的动作
senses.example: When I was young, we would walk to school together.
senses.exampleCN: 小时候我们常常一起走路上学。
senses.why: Habit is a small future repeated; the word marks each occasion without claiming permanence.
senses.whyCN: 习惯是被重复的小小将来；这个词标记每一次，而不主张永久。

senses.title: Probability
senses.definition: used to state what is likely, less certain than will
senses.definitionCN: 用来陈述可能性，比 will 更不确定
senses.example: It would be about five when they arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 他们到的时候大概是五点左右。
senses.why: Certainty is softened by the past form, so the statement stays a guess.
senses.whyCN: 过去式把确定性放软，于是这句话仍然只是猜测。

intro.en: Would is the past form of Old English willan, to wish, and still carries that wish in polite requests.
intro.cn: would 是古英语动词 willan「想要」的过去式，礼貌请求里仍然带着这层「想要」。

items.en: The verb willan meant to want or wish, and had its own past tense wolde.
items.cn: 动词 willan 意为想要、愿意，有自己的过去式 wolde。

items.en: Wolde covered both past wish and past habitual action, two senses that survive.
items.cn: wolde 既表过去的意愿，也表过去的习惯动作，两种含义都留存下来。

items.en: Middle English respelled wolde as would, and the l was later silenced in speech.
items.cn: 中古英语把 wolde 改拼为 would，后来口语里 l 不再发音。

items.en: Grammarians put would into conditional sentences as the standard form for unreality.
items.cn: 近代早期语法学家把 would 定为条件句中表示非现实的规范形式。

items.en: Modern English uses it for the past future, politeness, habits and speculation, one word with many mild duties.
items.cn: 现代英语用它表过去将来、礼貌、习惯与推测，一个词担着许多温和的职务。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the other modal and semi-modal forms; the near-meaning group holds expressions of willingness and habit.
note.cn: 形近组收其他情态与半情态形式；近义组收意愿与习惯的表达。

entries.definition: The present form of would, for a future that still may happen.
entries.definitionCN: 情态动词，义为「将、会」，仍是可能发生的将来。

entries.definition: A modal for future and offers, mainly formal British use.
entries.definitionCN: 情态动词，表将来与提议，多见于正式英式英语。

entries.definition: The past form of can, also used for politeness and possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 情态动词，can 的过去式，也用于礼貌与可能。

entries.definition: The past form of may, used for a weaker possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 情态动词，may 的过去式，表示更弱的可能。

entries.definition: The past of shall, but now mainly about duty or advice.
entries.definitionCN: 情态动词，shall 的过去式，如今主要表义务与建议。

entries.definition: The clearest way to describe a past habit.
entries.definitionCN: 半情态短语，义为「过去常常」，表旧习惯最清楚。

entries.definition: The full phrase for being ready to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「愿意做」，把意愿说全。

entries.definition: Wanting to be something, as in a would-be actor.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「想当……的」，如 would-be actor。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the idea of one step back from reality, which explains most uses of would.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「比现实退后一步」这一想法，它解释了 would 的大多数用法。

normal.en: Would is will stepped back one tense, and that step explains politeness and unreality.
normal.cn: would 是 will 退后一个时态，这一步解释了礼貌与虚拟。

normal.en: Would like to is the polite way to say want to.
normal.cn: would like to 是 want to 的客气说法。

normal.en: Would rather chooses, would sooner chooses more firmly.
normal.cn: would rather 是选择，would sooner 更坚决。

normal.en: Would have done describes the branch that was never taken.
normal.cn: would have done 描述那条从未走上的岔路。

normal.en: We would walk to school means we did it again and again.
normal.cn: we would walk to school 指我们反复这样做过。

abstract.en: Would is grammar’s way of leaving the room: it speaks about futures, habits and wishes without standing in them.
abstract.cn: would 是语法上的「抽身」：谈将来、习惯与愿望，却不站在其中。

abstract.en: Every polite request is a small fiction: the speaker pretends the answer is not yet fixed.
abstract.cn: 每个礼貌请求都是一点小小的虚构：说话人假装答案还没定。

abstract.en: One little word holds the open and the closed door at once: what would happen, and what would have.
abstract.cn: 这个小词同时握着开着与关着的门：将会发生什么，以及本来会发生什么。

examples.en: I said I would help, and I will.
examples.cn: 我说过我会帮忙，我就一定帮。

examples.en: Would you pass me the salt?
examples.cn: 请把盐递给我好吗？

examples.en: If I were taller, I would play basketball.
examples.cn: 要是我更高一些，就会去打篮球。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「捂的」——捂着嘴小声请求，语气软：会、愿意

root: 古英语动词 willan「想要」的过去式 wolde，中古英语改拼为 would；同源词有 will（动词与名词）、willing、would-be。

sensesIntro.en: Would works as past future, as willingness, as politeness, as unreality, as habit and as mild speculation.
sensesIntro.cn: would 可作过去将来、意愿、礼貌、虚拟、习惯与温和推测。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a fork, looking down the path not taken.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在岔路口，望着那条没走的路。

branches.en: TENSE LINE: the future as seen from the past.
branches.cn: 时态线：从过去看的将来。

branches.en: WILL LINE: willingness and refusal.
branches.cn: 意愿线：愿意与不肯。

branches.en: MANNER LINE: politeness through distance.
branches.cn: 方式线：用距离表达客气。

branches.en: SHADE LINE: unreality, habit and guesswork.
branches.cn: 语气线：虚拟、习惯与推测。

branches.en: CONTRAST: will is open future, would have is closed past.
branches.cn: 对照线：will 是敞开的将来，would have 是关上的过去。

intro.en: Would takes no affixes; its shortened form ’d is the only regular reduction.
intro.cn: would 不带词缀，唯一常见的缩略是 ’d。

latinIntro.en: No Latin enters here; the modal is a native Germanic verb form.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词里没有拉丁成分，它是日耳曼语本土的动词形式。

items.exampleCN: 它由 will 构成 willing。

items.example: It shows the modal as a bound form.
items.exampleCN: 它展示这个情态词的粘着用法。

definition_zh: 画廊；美术馆；楼座；走廊；一批收藏
definition_en: a room or building for showing art, or a raised seating area or long passage
core_image: 长廊两侧挂满画框，参观者缓步从一幅画走到另一幅
scene: 美术馆开门时阳光斜照进长廊。 A quiet gallery showed watercolours from thirty young painters this spring.
sceneCN: 这里 gallery 是「画廊；美术馆」（第 1 个义项：陈列艺术品的场所）；句意为今年春天一家安静的美术馆展出了三十位年轻画家的水彩画。

collocations.zh: 迎合大众口味博取喝彩

derivatives.zh: gallery 加 -ist 构成，义为「画廊经营者」
gallery 的意大利语式再借词，义为「拱廊商业街；购物廊」

senses.title: Room for showing art
senses.definition: a room or building where paintings and sculptures are shown
senses.definitionCN: 陈列绘画与雕塑的房间或建筑
senses.example: The city gallery is free on Sundays.
senses.exampleCN: 市立美术馆周日免费开放。
senses.why: The word first meant a long covered passage, and art hung along such walls, so the room sense grew there.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指带顶的长廊，画作就挂在这样的墙上，展示空间的义项由此生长。

senses.title: Raised seating tier
senses.definition: the highest balcony with the cheapest seats in a theatre
senses.definitionCN: 剧院里位置最高、票价最低的楼座
senses.example: Students watched the opera from the gallery.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们从楼座看歌剧。
senses.why: A long passage turns upward in a building; the gallery is literally the upper corridor of seats.
senses.whyCN: 长廊在建筑中向上转折，gallery 字面就是座位构成的高层走廊。

senses.title: Spectators collectively
senses.definition: the people watching, especially in court or a theatre
senses.definitionCN: 观看的人，尤指法庭或剧院中的旁听者
senses.example: The lawyer's joke woke the gallery.
senses.exampleCN: 律师的玩笑逗醒了旁听席。
senses.why: Seats name the seated; the tier label slid onto the people sitting there.
senses.whyCN: 座位可以代指就座者，楼座的称呼滑向了坐在那里的人。

senses.title: Underground passage in a mine
senses.definition: a horizontal tunnel dug in a mine
senses.definitionCN: 矿井中开凿的水平巷道
senses.example: The engineers walked the gallery to check the supports.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师们走过巷道检查支护。
senses.why: Mining kept the original covered-passage idea more literally than art did.
senses.whyCN: 采矿比艺术更直接地保留了「带顶长廊」的本义。

senses.title: Collection shown together
senses.definition: a set of pictures, photos, or items shown as a group
senses.definitionCN: 作为一组展示的图片或物品
senses.example: The website added a photo gallery of the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 网站添加了这次旅行的照片集。
senses.why: A room of paintings became a page of pictures; the grouping idea survived the screen.
senses.whyCN: 一间挂画的房间变成了一页图片，成组陈列的观念在屏幕时代延续。

intro.en: Gallery entered English from French and Italian, ultimately from a word for a great tank or store-room.
intro.cn: gallery 经法语与意大利语进入英语，最终源于意为「大蓄水池、储藏室」的词。

items.en: Italian galleria meant a long portico or passage, borrowed from medieval forms.
items.cn: 意大利语 galleria 指有柱廊的长通道，借自中世纪的形式。

items.en: Medieval Latin galeria is generally linked to galilea, a church porch, of disputed origin.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 galeria 一般认为与 galilea（教堂门廊）相关，来源有争议。

items.en: Old French galerie carried the passage sense into English speech.
items.cn: 古法语 galerie 带着通道义进入英语。

items.en: Middle English gallery at first meant a long covered walk or balcony.
items.cn: 中古英语 gallery 起初指带顶长廊或楼台。

items.en: Art display, theatre tiers, mine tunnels, and photo sets all kept the long-aisle image.
items.cn: 艺术陈列、剧院楼座、矿巷与图片集都保留了「长廊」意象。

note.en: Gallery overlaps with museum and hall, and hides a spelling trap in gallery vs galley.
note.cn: gallery 与 museum、hall 意义交叉，拼写上则要与 galley 区分。

entries.definition: a ship rowed by oars, or a ship's kitchen
entries.definitionCN: 桨帆船；船上的厨房；与 gallery 只差两个字母，词源无关

entries.definition: a covered shopping arcade
entries.definitionCN: 拱廊商业街；gallery 的意大利语式同源词

entries.definition: a waterproof overshoe
entries.definitionCN: 橡胶套鞋；拼写开头相近但词源无关

entries.definition: a building keeping and showing collections
entries.definitionCN: 博物馆；藏品更广，gallery 偏重陈列

entries.definition: a covered passage with shops
entries.definitionCN: 拱廊街；与 gallery 同源的商业分支

entries.definition: a raised platform or tier
entries.definitionCN: 楼台；与楼座义相邻

normalIntro.en: Five grounded hooks for gallery.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实词形的 gallery 记忆钩子。

normal.en: Gallery is a hall with a series of walls, and series appears in its pronunciation.
normal.cn: gallery 是带有一排排墙面的厅，读音里藏着 series 的意味。

normal.en: Play to the gallery means aiming jokes at the cheap seats.
normal.cn: play to the gallery 指迎合最便宜的楼座观众。

normal.en: Mine galleries are the passage sense kept underground.
normal.cn: 矿道 gallery 是「通道」本义留在地下的样子。

normal.en: A photo gallery is a wall of pictures moved onto a page.
normal.cn: photo gallery 是把挂画之墙搬到网页上。

normal.en: Do not confuse gallery with galley, the ship's kitchen.
normal.cn: 不要把 gallery 与船厨 galley 弄混。

abstract.en: Walk a long painted corridor: that walk is the word's skeleton.
abstract.cn: 走一条挂满画的长廊：这段行走就是词的骨架。

abstract.en: Hear the double l like two pillars holding a roof.
abstract.cn: 双写 l 像两根撑着屋顶的柱子。

abstract.en: Climb theatre stairs to the cheap top seats, the gallery's other face.
abstract.cn: 沿剧院台阶爬到顶层廉价座，那是 gallery 的另一张脸。

examples.en: Her paintings hang in a small gallery downtown.
examples.cn: 她的画挂在市中心一家小画廊里。

examples.en: We sat in the gallery and still heard every note.
examples.cn: 我们坐在楼座上，每个音符都听得见。

examples.en: The engineers inspected a flooded mine gallery.
examples.cn: 工程师检查了一条被水淹没的矿巷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「戛勒瑞」——画廊里挂了勒级的珍贵画卷，瑞气满堂。

root: 一般认为源于中世纪拉丁语 galeria（长廊），或与教会门廊 galilea 相关，来源存疑；核心意象始终是「带顶的长通道」。

sensesIntro.en: The long passage is the skeleton; art halls, theatre tiers, mine tunnels, and photo sets hang along it.
sensesIntro.cn: 长通道是骨架；艺术殿堂、剧院楼座、矿巷与图片集都沿它排开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long roofed aisle with things placed along it
core.cn: 核心意象：两侧排布展品的长廊

branches.en: art on walls and screens
branches.cn: 墙上与屏幕上的陈列

branches.en: the tier and its people
branches.cn: 楼座与其观众

branches.en: tunnels kept from the old sense
branches.cn: 保留古义的矿巷

branches.en: the public art space
branches.cn: 公共艺术空间

branches.en: audience as a single body
branches.cn: 作为整体的观众

intro.en: Gallery spawned one international offspring and many everyday phrases.
intro.cn: gallery 派生出一个国际化的后代词与许多日常短语。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin galeria is the recorded stop on the way into English.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 galeria 是该词进入英语途中被记录的一站。

items.example: Galeria is the earliest written ancestor here.
items.exampleCN: galeria 是这里可考的最早书面祖先。

items.example: Galilea named porches at some Italian churches.
items.exampleCN: galilea 曾指意大利一些教堂的门廊。

items.example: Milan's galleria is roofed in glass.
items.exampleCN: 米兰的拱廊街以玻璃封顶。

items.example: The -aria ending marks places in Italian borrowings.
items.exampleCN: -aria 词尾在意大利语借词中标记场所。

items.meaning: a set of pictures on show
items.example: The site updated its photo gallery.
Some politicians always play to the gallery.
items.exampleCN: 有些政客总是哗众取宠。

items.meaning: seats for visitors in court or parliament
