definition_en: how fast something moves, the quality of being fast, or to move or make something move faster
core_image: 汽车在空旷的公路上越开越快，路边的标牌向后飞掠成一片模糊
scene: 汽车在高速公路上加速。 The car gathered speed on the highway.

derivatives.zh: 迅速的
迅速地

senses.title: Rate of movement
senses.definition: the rate at which something moves
senses.definitionCN: 某物移动的速率
senses.example: The car gathered speed on the highway.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车在高速公路上加速。
senses.why: This is the central physical sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词核心的物理含义。

senses.title: The quality of being fast
senses.definition: the quality of moving or acting quickly

senses.example: She finished the work with great speed.

senses.why: Speed also names quickness itself, not only a number.

senses.title: To move fast
senses.definition: to move quickly, or to make something move faster
senses.definitionCN: 快速移动，或使某物移动得更快
senses.example: He sped away on his bike.
senses.exampleCN: 他骑着自行车疾驰而去。
senses.why: The verb turns the quality into an action.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这种性质变成动作。

intro.en: Speed first meant success, then quickness, then rate of movement.
intro.cn: speed 最初意为成功，后指迅速，再指移动的速度。

items.en: Sped meant success or prosperity.
items.cn: sped 意为成功或兴旺。

items.en: The word came to mean quickness, as success came fast.
items.cn: 由于成功来得快，这个词开始表示迅速。

items.en: Speed came to mean the rate of motion.
items.cn: speed 开始表示运动的速率。

items.en: Speed limit gave it a legal sense.
items.cn: speed limit 赋予它法律含义。

items.en: To speed up became the common verb of hurrying.
items.cn: speed up 成为常用的催促动词。

normal.en: The train reached its top speed.

abstract.en: Speed compresses time into distance.
abstract.cn: 速度把时间压缩成距离。

abstract.en: The faster we move, the less we see.
abstract.cn: 移动得越快，看见的越少。

abstract.en: Hurry is speed without direction.
abstract.cn: 匆忙是没有方向的速度。

sensesIntro.en: Speed means the rate of movement, quickness, or to move faster.

core.en: Distance divided by the time it takes.
core.cn: 距离除以所花的时间。

branches.en: A car pushes faster along an open road.

branches.en: Hands finish a task before the clock expects.

branches.en: A bicycle rushes past a gate.

branches.en: The measure and the hurrying act share one word.
branches.cn: 度量与疾驰的动作共用一个词。

branches.en: Quickness in work and movement both look like speed.

intro.en: Speed forms adjectives, adverbs, and measuring devices.
intro.cn: speed 构成形容词、副词和测量装置。

latinIntro.en: Speed is Germanic and has no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: speed 属日耳曼语，没有拉丁词根。

definition_zh: 在……期间；在……持续的时间内
definition_en: all through a period of time, or at some point within it
core_image: 一条时间带被整个罩住
scene: 漫长的暑假里，小屋的花园被雨水浇得一片浓绿。 The garden stayed green during the whole summer holiday.
sceneCN: 这里 during 是「在……期间」（第 1 个义项：贯穿某段时间）；句意：整个暑假期间花园一直保持翠绿。

derivatives.zh: 同源动词，义为「忍受；持续」
同源名词，义为「持续时间」

senses.title: All through a period
senses.definition: from the beginning to the end of a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 从某段时间的开头持续到结尾
senses.example: The garden stayed green during the whole summer.
senses.exampleCN: 整个夏天花园一直保持翠绿。
senses.why: The preposition covers a band of time like a roof over it.
senses.whyCN: 这个介词像屋顶一样罩住整段时间带。

senses.title: At some point within a period
senses.definition: at a moment inside the stated period
senses.definitionCN: 在所述时段之内的某个时刻
senses.example: She woke twice during the night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里她醒了两次。
senses.why: The roof also covers one point that sits inside the band.
senses.whyCN: 这层屋顶同样罩住位于时段内的某一点。

intro.en: During is the present participle of an old verb of lasting, hardened into a preposition.
intro.cn: during 原是一个表示「持续」的古老动词的现在分词，后来固化成介词。

items.en: Old French durer meant to last, from Latin durare.
items.cn: 古法语 durer 意为持续，来自拉丁语 durare。

items.en: Latin durare meant to harden or endure, the root behind durable and duration.
items.cn: 拉丁语 durare 意为变硬、持续，是 durable 与 duration 的词根。

items.en: Middle English kept endure as a verb and used during as its participle, meaning while lasting.
items.cn: 中古英语保留动词 endure，并用 during 作其分词，意为「在持续期间」。

items.en: Gradually during stopped needing a verb and worked alone as a preposition.
items.cn: 渐渐地 during 不再依附动词，独立充当介词。

items.en: Modern English fixed it as the standard preposition for periods of time.
items.cn: 现代英语把它定型为表示时间段的标准介词。

note.en: These words stand near during in form or in meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 during 相邻。

entries.definitionCN: 忍受；持续

entries.definition: the length of time something lasts

normal.en: duration is how long something lasts.
normal.cn: duration 指某事持续多久。

normal.en: during the night can mean one moment inside the night.

normal.en: during the whole summer covers every day of it.

abstract.en: See a ribbon of time with a roof stretched over all of it.

abstract.en: Feel one raindrop hitting somewhere inside the covered band.
abstract.cn: 感受一滴雨落在被罩住的时间带内某处。

abstract.en: Watch the calendar pages flip while the roof stays firm.
abstract.cn: 看日历一页页翻过，而屋顶始终不移。

examples.en: Please stay seated during the film.
examples.cn: 放映期间请留在座位上。

examples.en: During the storm, the lights went out twice.
examples.cn: 暴风雨期间，电灯熄了两次。

examples.en: He read many books during his last year at school.
examples.cn: 在校最后一年里他读了许多书。

definition_zh: 池塘；鱼塘；养殖池；冷却池；大西洋（口语）
definition_en: a small area of still water, often made by people; also a managed basin for fish or for industrial water, and informally the Atlantic Ocean
core_image: 一圈土堤围住的一小片静水，水面映着低垂的柳枝
scene: 夏末的午后，村口的柳树把影子投在水面上，几只鸭子慢慢划过。 Behind the mill, willow branches hung low over a quiet pond.
sceneCN: 这里的 pond 是「池塘」（第 1 个义项：小片静水）；句意为磨坊后面，柳枝低低地垂在一片安静的池塘上。图中可辨识物件：柳枝、水面、鸭子。

pos.zh: 池塘；鱼塘；养殖池；冷却池；大西洋（口语）

derivatives.zh: 由 pond 与 weed 复合而成，义为「池草；眼子菜类水草」
由 pond 与 side 复合而成，义为「池边的」
由 fish 与 pond 复合而成，义为「鱼塘」

senses.title: A small area of still water
senses.definition: a small area of still water, usually smaller than a lake and often dug or dammed by people
senses.definitionCN: 一片不大的静水，通常比湖小，多为人工挖成或筑堤蓄成
senses.example: Ducks floated quietly on the village pond.
senses.exampleCN: 鸭子静静地浮在村子的池塘上。
senses.why: The word began as a name for an enclosed place, and when the fence became an earth bank the same name settled on the water held inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指被围起来的地方；当围栏变成土堤，同一个名字就落到了被围在里面的水上。

senses.title: A basin kept for fish or waterfowl
senses.definition: a pond built or managed so that fish, ducks or other water animals can be raised in it
senses.definitionCN: 为养鱼、养鸭或其他水生动物而修建、管理的水体
senses.example: They dug three ponds behind the house for carp.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在屋后挖了三口鱼塘养鲤鱼。
senses.why: Once water could be held in one place, it could also be stocked, so the word widened from a patch of water to a working basin with a harvest.
senses.whyCN: 水一旦能被蓄在一处，就能往里放养生物，于是词义从一片水面扩展到有收成的生产水体。

senses.title: An engineered basin for a process
senses.definition: a basin built to hold water for cooling, settling or storing waste in an industrial process
senses.definitionCN: 工业生产中用来冷却、沉淀或存放废水的池子
senses.example: The plant pumps warm water into a cooling pond.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂把温水抽进冷却池。
senses.why: Industry borrowed the word for any shallow basin that holds liquid, keeping the old shape of water shut in by a rim.
senses.whyCN: 工业借用了这个词来指任何盛液体的浅池，保留的仍是「水被边沿围住」这一古老形状。

senses.title: The Atlantic, in casual speech
senses.definition: the Atlantic Ocean, used informally by people on one side of it when speaking of the other side
senses.definitionCN: 大西洋的口语说法，岸这边的人用它来指对岸
senses.example: She moved across the pond twenty years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 她二十年前搬到了大西洋对岸。
senses.why: Calling an ocean a pond is a deliberate understatement: two shores are treated as the banks of one small sheet of water, which makes the distance sound crossable.
senses.whyCN: 把大洋叫作池塘是故意的轻描淡写：两岸被当成一小片水的两个边，遥远的距离听起来就像能一步跨过。

intro.en: Pond first named a fenced place, then the water held behind a bank, and only later any small still water.
intro.cn: pond 最早指围起来的地方，随后指土堤拦住的水，最后才泛指任何小片静水。

items.en: The element pund- appears in pundfald, a pen for stray cattle, and meant an enclosed place rather than water.
items.cn: 古英语中的 pund- 见于 pundfald（关牲口的围栏），指的是被围起来的地方，与水无关。

items.en: Middle English ponde named an artificial body of water, typically a small lake held back by an earth bank.
items.cn: 中古英语的 ponde 指人工蓄起的水体，通常是被土堤拦住的小湖。

items.en: The enclosing fence of the old word was replaced by the bank of the pond, so the boundary stayed and the contents changed from animals to water.
items.cn: 旧词里围住场地的栅栏被池塘的土堤取代，边界还在，围住的东西却从牲口变成了水。

items.en: Modern English pond covers any small still water, whether dug for gardens, stocked with fish or built for a factory.
items.cn: 现代英语的 pond 泛指任何小片静水，无论是为花园挖的、养鱼的，还是给工厂建的。

items.en: The teasing phrase across the pond turns the Atlantic into a small sheet of water, and compounds such as cooling pond extend the word to industry.
items.cn: 玩笑说法 across the pond 把大西洋说成一小片水；cooling pond 这类复合词则把词义延伸到工业。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short English words that differ from pond by a single letter; the near-meaning group gathers other names for still water.
note.cn: 形近组收与 pond 只差一两个字母的短词；近义组收其他表示静水的词。

entries.definition: A unit of weight or money, or an enclosure for animals; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 重量或货币单位，也指关动物的围栏；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Feeling affection or liking for someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 喜爱某人的；钟情的。

entries.definition: Something that ties people together, or a certificate of debt.
entries.definitionCN: 纽带；债券。

entries.definition: A sum of money kept for a special purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定用途保存的一笔钱；基金。

entries.definition: A lake or a small sheet of still water, now mostly used in literary writing and place names.
entries.definitionCN: 湖或小片静水，如今多见于文学描写与地名。

entries.definition: A small shallow patch of rainwater on the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 地面上由雨水积成的小浅水洼。

entries.definition: A large area of water surrounded by land.
entries.definitionCN: 被陆地环绕的大片水域；湖。

entries.definition: A large artificial lake used for storing water.
entries.definitionCN: 用于蓄水的大型人工湖；水库。

normalIntro.en: Pond is a word about a boundary: an enclosed place became an enclosed sheet of water, and the compounds show what people keep inside it.
normalIntro.cn: pond 是一个关于边界的词：被围住的地方变成了被围住的水面，而各类复合词则显示人们往里面放什么。

normal.en: Old English pundfald was a pen for cattle, so the earliest sense of the family is a fenced space, not a wet one.
normal.cn: 古英语 pundfald 是关牛的围栏，所以这一族词最早的意思是围起来的空间，而不是水。

normal.en: A pond is what you get when the fence around a place is replaced by a bank around water.
normal.cn: 当围住场地的栅栏换成围住水的土堤，得到的就是 pond。

normal.en: Fishpond and duck pond simply name the animals kept inside, which is the cheapest way to remember the word.
normal.cn: fishpond 与 duck pond 直接把养在里面的动物写出来，这是记住这个词最省力的办法。

normal.en: Pondweed grows where ponds are, so the compound -weed tells you the plant's home rather than its shape.
normal.cn: pondweed 长在池塘里，所以 -weed 这个复合成分告诉你的是植物的住处，而不是它的形状。

normal.en: Across the pond works because two coasts can be imagined as the two banks of one small stretch of water.
normal.cn: across the pond 之所以成立，是因为两岸可以被想象成一小片水的两个岸。

abstract.en: Every pond is a decision to stop water from moving on, which is why the word sits so close to dams and banks.
abstract.cn: 每个池塘都是「不让水继续流走」的决定，所以这个词总跟堤坝、岸沿挨在一起。

abstract.en: A word that once meant a fence now means a surface, a sign that boundaries outlive the things they were built for.
abstract.cn: 一个曾指栅栏的词如今指一片水面，说明边界往往比它当初围的东西活得更久。

abstract.en: Shrinking an ocean to a pond is language doing what maps cannot: making distance feel small enough to joke about.
abstract.cn: 把大洋缩成池塘，是语言做了地图做不到的事：让距离小到可以拿来开玩笑。

examples.en: The farm keeps a pond for ducks and carp.
examples.cn: 这个农场留了一口池塘养鸭子和鲤鱼。

examples.en: Willow branches brushed the surface of the pond.
examples.cn: 柳枝拂过池塘的水面。

examples.en: Her sister has lived across the pond for years.
examples.cn: 她姐姐在大西洋对岸住了很多年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「胖得」——池塘里的鸭子吃得好，胖得游不动；记住 pond 是池塘。

root: 古英语 pund- 表示「围起来的地方」（见 pundfald「关牲口的围栏」），中古英语 ponde 转指被土堤围住的水，后来泛指小片静水；更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a small sheet of still water; the branches add what the water is kept for, and one loose figurative use turns the Atlantic into a pond.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是一小片静水；各分支补出蓄水是为了什么，另有一处松散的比喻用法把大西洋说成池塘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a low earth bank holding a small sheet of quiet water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道低低的土堤围住一小片安静的水。

branches.en: a duck gliding across a village pond at dusk
branches.cn: 黄昏时一只鸭子划过村口的池塘

branches.en: a net lifted dripping from a fish pond

senses.why: The plant makes soft white balls, like little clouds on the field.

senses.title: Cloth or thread made from the fibre
senses.definition: thread or cloth woven from cotton fibre

senses.why: The fibre is spun and woven, so the word covers the cloth too.

senses.title: The cotton plant itself

senses.example: Bees buzzed over the cotton growing near the village.

definition_zh: 一双；一对；一对人；一对动物；配对
definition_en: two things or people that belong together, or to put two such things together
core_image: 两只一模一样的手套并排放着，指尖对着指尖
scene: 清晨的门口，两只沾了泥的靴子被人并排放好，鞋尖朝外。 She could not find the pair of gloves that matched her coat.
sceneCN: 这里 pair 是「一双、一对配套的东西」（第 1 个义项：成对使用的两件物品）；句意是她找不到和外套相配的那副手套。图中可辨识的物件：门口的靴子、泥点、手套。

pos.zh: 一双；一对；一对人；一对动物

derivatives.zh: 由 pair 加 -ed 构成，义为「成对的；配对的」
由 pair 加 -ing 构成，义为「配对；搭配」

由 pair 与 -wise 复合而成，义为「成对地；两两之间地」

senses.title: Two things that go together
senses.definition: two things of the same kind that are used together or look the same
senses.definitionCN: 同一种类、搭配使用或看起来相配的两件东西
senses.example: She could not find the pair of gloves that matched her coat.
senses.exampleCN: 她找不到和外套相配的那副手套。
senses.why: Latin paria were equal things, so the word starts from two items that answer each other, not from any particular object.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 paria 指「相等的东西」，所以这个词的起点是两件彼此对应的物品，而不是某种特定的东西。

senses.title: Two people linked together
senses.definition: two people who are connected by love, work or a shared activity
senses.definitionCN: 因感情、工作或共同活动而连在一起的两个人
senses.example: The pair have worked in the same lab for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个人在同一间实验室共事了十年。
senses.why: Since paria means equals, the word easily moves from matching objects to two people who are matched in some role.
senses.whyCN: 既然 paria 意为「相等之物」，这个词就很容易从相配的物品转到在某种角色上相配的两个人。

senses.title: Two animals kept together
senses.definition: a male and a female animal, or two animals of the same kind, kept together
senses.definitionCN: 养在一起的一雌一雄，或同种的两只动物
senses.example: The farm bought a pair of geese for the pond.
senses.exampleCN: 农场为池塘买了一对鹅。
senses.why: Breeding needs two, and the old sense of equal things fits a male and female kept together for mating.
senses.whyCN: 繁殖需要两个，而「相等之物」的老义正好贴合为交配而养在一起的一雄一雌。

senses.title: To put two things together
senses.definition: to join two things or people so that they form a matching set or a working team
senses.definitionCN: 把两件东西或两个人组合起来，成为相配的一套或一个搭档
senses.example: Students were paired by level for the speaking test.
senses.exampleCN: 口语考试按水平把学生两人一组配对。
senses.why: Once a pair names a set of two, the verb simply performs the action of making that set exist.
senses.whyCN: 既然 pair 指「两个组成的一套」，动词就是让这样一套真正形成的动作。

intro.en: Pair comes from Latin words for equal things, which passed through French and came to name any two items that answer each other.
intro.cn: pair 来自拉丁语中表示「相等之物」的词，经法语传来，后来指任何彼此对应的两件东西。

items.en: Par meant equal or a match, and it is the stem behind a family of words about being level.
items.cn: par 意为相等的、对等的，是整族表示「持平」的词背后的词干。

items.en: The neuter plural paria named equal things taken together, which is the form the noun needed.
items.cn: 中性复数 paria 指放在一起的相等之物，正好是名词所需的形式。

items.en: Old French paire kept the sense of a set of two matching things.
items.cn: 古法语 paire 保留了「相配的两件成一套」的意思。

items.en: Middle English pair widened from matching objects to couples, partners and animals kept together.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pair 从相配的物品扩展到伴侣、搭档和养在一起的动物。

items.en: Modern English uses pair as a noun for any matched two and as a verb for the act of matching.
items.cn: 现代英语把 pair 用作名词指任何相配的两个，也用作动词指配对的动作。

note.en: The look-alike group collects relatives of the Latin stem for equal; the near-meaning group collects words for twos and partners.
note.cn: 形近组收「相等」这一拉丁词干的同族词；近义组收表示「两个」与「搭档」的词。

entries.definition: An equal level or standard, as in the phrase on par with.
entries.definitionCN: 相等的水平或标准，如短语 on par with。

entries.definition: The state of being equal in rank or value.
entries.definitionCN: 地位或价值相等的状态。

entries.definition: To set two things side by side to see how they differ.

entries.definition: Two people together, or two of the same thing.

entries.definition: Two people who perform or work together.

entries.definition: One of two things that go well together.
entries.definitionCN: 相配的两件中的一件。

entries.definition: One of two children born at the same time, or one of a matching set.
entries.definitionCN: 双胞胎之一，或相配一对中的一个。

normalIntro.en: Pair rests on a Latin word for equal, so the whole family is about two things that stand level with each other.
normalIntro.cn: pair 依托拉丁语中表示「相等」的词，所以整族词都围绕「彼此持平的两样东西」。

normal.en: Latin par means equal, and paria is its plural for equal things, which is exactly what a pair is.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 par 意为相等，paria 是它的复数，指相等之物，正是一对的意思。

normal.en: Parity, par and compare all keep the equal part of the same stem.
normal.cn: parity、par 和 compare 都保留着同一词干里「相等」的那部分。

normal.en: Pair up adds a particle that turns the noun into the action of forming a set.
normal.cn: pair up 加上一个小词，就把名词变成「组成一套」的动作。

normal.en: In pairs uses the plural to mean two at a time, a pattern that appears in classrooms and queues.
normal.cn: in pairs 用复数表示「一次两个」，课堂和排队时都常见。

normal.en: A pair of shoes works because the two shoes answer each other, not because there are simply two shoes.
normal.cn: 一双鞋之所以成双，是因为两只鞋彼此对应，而不是因为刚好有两只鞋。

abstract.en: Two equal things need each other to be a pair, which is why the word carries a quiet idea of balance.
abstract.cn: 两个相等之物要彼此依存才成对，所以这个词暗暗带着平衡的意味。

abstract.en: Pairing is a way of organising the world by twos, from shoes to lab partners.
abstract.cn: 配对是把世界按「两个」来整理的一种方式，从鞋子到实验搭档都一样。

abstract.en: A word born from equality reminds us that a pair only works when both sides count.
abstract.cn: 一个从「相等」生出的词提醒人：一对要成立，两边都得算数。

examples.en: She could not find the pair of gloves that matched her coat.
examples.cn: 她找不到和外套相配的那副手套。

sensesIntro.en: The core is two things standing equal to each other; the senses spread to objects used together, linked people, animals kept as a pair, and the act of matching.

definition_zh: 想；思考；认为；回想；打算
definition_en: to use the mind to form ideas, opinions, or plans, or to hold something as an opinion
core_image: 头脑里的工作台：想法在上面被拿起、翻看、装配
scene: 窗外下着雨,她盯着棋盘很久。 Think before you move the knight.
sceneCN: 这里 think 是「思考」（第 1 个义项：用心智形成想法）；句意：走马之前先想一想。

pos.zh: 思考；想法（口语，如 have a think）

derivatives.zh: 想法；思想；思考（think 的过去式转名词）

senses.title: To use the mind
senses.definition: to use the mind to form ideas, solve problems, or make decisions
senses.definitionCN: 运用头脑形成想法、解决问题或作出决定
senses.example: Give me a minute to think.
senses.exampleCN: 给我一分钟想一想。
senses.why: The core act: the mind works visibly hard, and the word simply names that work.
senses.whyCN: 核心行为：头脑明显地在劳作，这个词就是给这份劳作起名。

senses.title: To hold an opinion
senses.definition: to believe or hold something as an opinion, often less certain than know
senses.definitionCN: 相信或把某事当作看法，确定性低于 know
senses.example: I think the meeting starts at nine.
senses.exampleCN: 我想会议九点开始。
senses.why: An idea formed in the head is offered to the world as a claim; think marks the claim as personal and revisable.
senses.whyCN: 在头脑中形成的想法被作为主张交给世界；think 标记这主张属个人且可修正。

senses.title: To recall or imagine
senses.definition: to bring a past thing to mind, or to form a picture of something not present
senses.definitionCN: 让往事浮现心头，或构想不在眼前之物
senses.example: She still thinks of that summer by the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 她仍会想起海边那个夏天。
senses.why: The mind's workbench holds not only the present but the past and the possible; both arrive by the same act.
senses.whyCN: 头脑的工作台不只放当下，也放过去与可能；两者经由同一个动作到来。

senses.title: To intend or plan
senses.definition: to have a plan or intention in the mind, often in thinking of doing
senses.definitionCN: 心中存有计划或意图，常用于 thinking of doing
senses.example: We are thinking of moving to the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在考虑搬到海边住。
senses.why: A plan is an action rehearsed in the head before it happens; thinking is that rehearsal.
senses.whyCN: 计划是行动在头脑中的预演；thinking 就是这场预演。

senses.title: To expect or suppose
senses.definition: to expect or suppose that something will happen or is true
senses.definitionCN: 预期某事会发生或属实
senses.example: I think it will clear up by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 我料想到中午天会放晴。
senses.why: Opinion pointed forward becomes expectation: the same claim, wearing tomorrow's clothes.
senses.whyCN: 看法指向未来便成了预期：同一个主张，换上了明天的衣裳。

intro.en: Think is a native Germanic verb, and its strange past form thought preserves a very old sound pattern in which a t replaced the k of the present.
intro.cn: think 是日耳曼本土动词；其奇特的过去式 thought 保留了一种极古老的音变模式：过去式以 t 代替现在的 k。

items.en: The common Germanic root Thankjan meant to seem or to appear to the mind; the same root gave both think and seem in some relatives.
items.cn: 公认日耳曼词根 Thankjan 意为「在心中显现、似乎」；同一词根在部分亲属语言中既给出 think 也给出 seem 义。

items.en: Old English had two verbs: Thencan, to think in the modern sense, and Thyncan, to seem. Their past forms crossed and merged.
items.cn: 古英语有两个动词：Thencan（现代的「想」）与 Thyncan（「似乎」）；二者的过去式相互交叉并合流。

items.en: Middle English merged the two verbs into think with past thought, and the seeming sense faded away.
items.cn: 中古英语将两词合并为 think，过去式 thought，「似乎」义渐消。

items.en: Modern English fixed the paradigm think, thought and built a wide family: thinker, thoughtful, thoughtless, overthink.
items.cn: 现代英语固定 think-thought 范式，并衍生出 thinker、thoughtful、thoughtless、overthink 等庞大家族。

items.en: The noun think (have a think) and think tank show the verb moving into noun jobs in modern colloquial and institutional English.
items.cn: 名词 think（have a think）与 think tank 显示该动词在现代口语与机构用语中转任名词。

note.en: The first group is the think-thought family; the second compares verbs of mind work.
note.cn: 第一组是 think-thought 词族；第二组比较各种「心智劳作」动词。

entries.definitionCN: think 的过去式，也可作名词指想法

entries.definition: an object; shares most sounds with think but is a different word entirely
entries.definitionCN: 东西；与 think 读音相近，但完全是另一个词

entries.definitionCN: 感谢；出自关于内心感受的相关日耳曼词根

entries.definition: to accept something as true; stronger commitment than think
entries.definitionCN: 相信；比 think 承诺更强

entries.definition: to think about carefully before deciding
entries.definitionCN: 斟酌；决定前的仔细思考

entries.definition: to assume something is true without proof
entries.definitionCN: 假定；设想（无充分证据的认定）

normalIntro.en: Real hooks: the old t-past pattern, the think-thought family, and the difference between think and know.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：古老的 t 形过去式、think-thought 词族、以及 think 与 know 之别。

normal.en: Think, thought, thought: the k becomes ght in the past, an ancient fingerprint.
normal.cn: think 的过去式 thought：k 变 ght，是古老的指纹。

normal.en: I think softens a claim; I know hardens it.
normal.cn: I think 让主张变软，I know 让主张变硬。

normal.en: Think of recalls, think about studies, think over weighs.
normal.cn: think of 是想起，think about 是研究，think over 是掂量。

normal.en: A think tank is a tank full of thinking, not of fuel.
normal.cn: think tank 是装满思考的罐子，不是装燃料的。

normal.en: Thoughtful people think of others as well as of problems.
normal.cn: thoughtful 的人既想问题，也想别人。

abstract.en: Thinking is the rehearsal room where actions try their lines.
abstract.cn: 思考是排练厅，行动在里面练习台词。

abstract.en: Every thought is a small claim asking to be tested.
abstract.cn: 每个想法都是一桩等待检验的小主张。

abstract.en: The mind's workbench never quite empties.
abstract.cn: 头脑的工作台从不清空。

examples.en: She sat quietly, thinking about the offer.
examples.cn: 她静静坐着，考虑那份邀约。

examples.en: I thought the train left at noon, but it was three.
examples.cn: 我以为火车中午开，其实是三点。

examples.en: He thought carefully before answering.
examples.cn: 他仔细想过才回答。

sensesIntro.en: Think works the mind in five directions: solving, opining, recalling, planning, and expecting, all from one image of ideas handled on an inner workbench.
sensesIntro.cn: think 让心智朝五个方向运作：解题、持论、追忆、筹划、预期——全部来自「内在工作台上摆弄想法」这一个意象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an inner workbench where ideas are picked up, turned over, and assembled.
core.cn: 核心意象：内在工作台，想法在上面被拿起、翻看、装配。

branches.en: The bare labour of the mind.
branches.cn: 心智的朴素劳作。

branches.en: A claim offered as personal and revisable.
branches.cn: 作为个人可修正意见提出的主张。

branches.en: The workbench reaching into past and possibility.
branches.cn: 伸向过去与可能的工作台。

branches.en: Actions rehearsed before they happen.
branches.cn: 行动发生前的预演。

branches.en: Opinion dressed for tomorrow.
branches.cn: 换上明天衣裳的看法。

intro.en: Think builds its family with small native endings and compounds, mostly through its past form thought.
intro.cn: think 用本土小词尾与复合词构建词族，大多经由其过去式 thought。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source; the family is native Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.

definition_zh: 厚的；粗的；浓的；浓密的；愚蠢的；雾重的
definition_en: having a large distance between two sides, densely packed, not flowing easily, or slow to understand
core_image: 两大平面之间塞满了东西：一掌压不下去的厚
scene: 大雪整夜未停，清晨推开院门，积雪没了脚踝。 The snow lay thick on the garden path.
sceneCN: 这里 thick 是「厚厚地积着、浓密」（第 3 个义项：密集铺满）；句意：花园小径上积雪很厚。

derivatives.zh: 厚厚地；浓密地（thick 加副词后缀 -ly）
厚度；浓度；层（thick 加名词后缀 -ness）
使变厚；变浓（thick 加动词后缀 -en）
增稠剂（thicken 加施动者后缀 -er）

senses.title: Large between two surfaces
senses.definition: having a large distance between two opposite sides or surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 两个相对的面之间距离较大
senses.example: She wore a thick coat against the winter wind.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿上厚外套抵御寒风。
senses.why: The basic measure: a slab is thick when its two faces stand far apart, so the word names size across rather than along.
senses.whyCN: 最基本的量度：一块板的两面离得远就叫厚，这个词量的是横向的尺寸而不是纵向的。

senses.title: Densely packed together
senses.definition: growing or standing close together in large numbers
senses.definitionCN: 大量生长或聚集在一起，间距很小
senses.example: The forest is thick with pines and moss.
senses.exampleCN: 森林里松树和苔藓长得很密。
senses.why: When many things fill a space so closely that light struggles through, the crowding itself feels like thickness.
senses.whyCN: 当许多东西挤满一个空间、连光都难以穿过时，这种拥挤本身就让人感觉「厚」。

senses.title: Not flowing easily
senses.definition: (of a liquid) not flowing easily because it is dense or heavy
senses.definitionCN: 指液体浓稠、不易流动
senses.example: The sauce boiled down until it was thick and glossy.
senses.exampleCN: 酱汁熬到浓稠发亮。
senses.why: A dense liquid resists movement the way a thick plank resists bending, so the same word covers both blocks and broths.
senses.whyCN: 浓稠的液体抗拒流动，就像厚板抗拒弯折，同一个词便同时盖住了板块与汤汁。

senses.title: Slow to understand
senses.definition: (informal) not quick to understand, a little stupid
senses.definitionCN: （口语）理解得慢，有点迟钝
senses.example: Don't be thick, the answer is staring at you.
senses.exampleCN: 别犯迷糊了，答案就明摆在你眼前。
senses.why: An idea slides off a head as light slides off fog; the dense mind, like dense air, lets little through.
senses.whyCN: 想法滑不过一个脑袋，正如光穿不透浓雾；迟钝的头脑与浓重的空气一样，透不进多少东西。

senses.title: Heavy and hard to see through
senses.definition: (of fog, smoke, or air) heavy and difficult to see or breathe through
senses.definitionCN: 指雾、烟或空气浓重，难以看透或呼吸
senses.example: Thick smoke rolled down the stairwell.
senses.exampleCN: 浓烟涌下楼梯间。
senses.why: Smoke and fog fill space the way timber fills a wall, so seeing through them becomes as hard as drilling through a board.
senses.whyCN: 烟雾像木头填满墙壁一样填满空间，看穿它便变得像钻穿木板一样困难。

intro.en: Thick is a native Germanic word, old at the root: it goes back to an ancient word for densely pressed or crowded, and its cousins are found across the Germanic languages.
intro.cn: thick 是日耳曼本土词，词根十分古老：它追溯到表示「挤压密集」的古代词形，同源词遍布各日耳曼语言。

items.en: The common Germanic root is Theku, generally reconstructed as meaning thick, pressed close, or crowded; it had no Latin relatives.
items.cn: 公认的日耳曼词根一般重构为 Theku，意为「厚的、挤压紧密的、拥挤的」；它没有拉丁语同源词。

items.en: Old English Thicce already carried the main senses: solid in size, crowded in number, and heavy in texture.
items.cn: 古英语 Thicce 已具备主要义项：体积厚实、数量密集、质地浓重。

items.en: Norse Pokkr, a close cousin, reinforced the northern forms of the adjective.
items.cn: 古诺斯语的近亲词 Pokkr 加强了这一形容词在北方的形式。

items.en: Middle English thikke spread the figurative uses, and the adverb thikke(or thick) without -ly entered common speech.
items.cn: 中古英语 thikke 发展出比喻用法，无 -ly 的副词形式也进入日常口语。

items.en: Modern English fixed thick, thickly and thickness, and the idioms through thick and thin and thick as thieves gave the word a social flavour.
items.cn: 现代英语固定了 thick、thickly 与 thickness，习语 through thick and thin 和 thick as thieves 又给这个词添了人情味。

note.en: The first group holds the thick word family; the second compares adjectives of density and slowness.
note.cn: 第一组是 thick 词族；第二组比较表示密度与迟钝的形容词。

entries.definitionCN: 使变厚；变浓（thick 的动词形式）

entries.definition: the measure of how thick something is
entries.definitionCN: 厚度；浓度（thick 的名词形式）

entries.definition: a clever act meant to deceive; only one letter from thick, no relation in meaning
entries.definitionCN: 诡计；与 thick 仅一字母之差，词义无关

entries.definition: packed closely together; formal partner of the crowded sense of thick
entries.definitionCN: 稠密的；thick 密集义的正式对应词

entries.definition: of great weight or force; overlaps with thick smoke and thick weather
entries.definitionCN: 沉重的；在浓烟、恶劣天气等用法上与 thick 交叠

entries.definition: not quick to understand; politer than the informal sense of thick
entries.definitionCN: 迟缓的；比 thick 的迟钝义更委婉

normalIntro.en: Real hooks: the Germanic root of pressed-together, the thick family, and two famous idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：日耳曼「挤压密集」词根、thick 词族、以及两大著名习语。

normal.en: One image covers all senses: so much stuff that nothing moves easily.
normal.cn: 一个意象贯穿各义：东西多到什么都动弹不得。

normal.en: Thick fog, thick soup, thick forest: all hard to see through or push through.
normal.cn: 浓雾、浓汤、密林：都难以看穿或穿过。

normal.en: Through thick and thin once meant through forest and open ground.
normal.cn: through thick and thin 原指穿过密林与空地。

normal.en: Thick as thieves: as close and crowded together as partners in crime.
normal.cn: thick as thieves：像同伙一样亲密无间。

normal.en: Thicken the soup: the -en suffix turns the adjective into a verb.
normal.cn: thicken the soup：后缀 -en 把形容词变成动词。

abstract.en: Thick is the world pressing in from two sides at once.
abstract.cn: thick 是世界从两面同时挤进来的感觉。

abstract.en: A thick mind is a wall; a thick book is a door.
abstract.cn: 迟钝的头脑是墙，厚厚的书是门。

abstract.en: Where thin divides, thick protects.
abstract.cn: thin 分隔，thick 庇护。

examples.en: The walls are nearly a metre thick.
examples.cn: 这墙几乎有一米厚。

examples.en: A thick fog covered the harbour all morning.
examples.cn: 浓雾整个上午笼罩着海港。

examples.en: Her accent was thick with the sounds of her hometown.
examples.cn: 她的口音带着浓重的乡音。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「希克」——厚得只透一丝缝隙 → thick 厚的；浓的

root: 日耳曼本土词：原始日耳曼语词根（一般认为重构为 Theku，意为挤压密集）→ 古英语 Thicce「厚的、密的、浓的」，与德语 dick、荷兰语 dik 同源；无拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: Thick measures size across a slab, then spreads to crowding, to dense liquids and smoke, and finally, with a smile, to a slow head.
sensesIntro.cn: thick 先量板子的厚度，再延伸到拥挤、浓稠的液体与烟雾，最后带笑指向迟钝的脑袋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two faces pressed far apart, so full that nothing slips through.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个面被撑得很开，塞得满满，什么也穿不过。

branches.en: The physical measure of a slab or a wall.
branches.cn: 板与墙的物理厚度。

branches.en: Crowding that fills space like solid matter.
branches.cn: 像固体一样填满空间的拥挤。

branches.en: Liquids too dense to run freely.
branches.cn: 浓稠难流的液体。

branches.en: Fog that blocks the eye, a head that blocks the idea.
branches.cn: 挡住视线的雾，挡住想法的头脑。

branches.en: Both rest on one resistance: the world refusing to yield.
branches.cn: 两者立于同一种抗拒：世界拒绝让步。

intro.en: Thick is a bare Germanic root; English keeps it productive with small native suffixes like -en, -ness and -ly.
intro.cn: thick 是光秃秃的日耳曼词根；英语用 -en、-ness、-ly 等本土小后缀让它保持能产。

items.meaning: through good and bad times alike

definition_zh: 愚蠢的；傻；笨
definition_en: showing a lack of good sense, or slow to understand

senses.why: Anger lends the word a casual use.

intro.en: Stupid comes from a Latin word meaning stunned.
intro.cn: stupid 来自拉丁语词，意为被惊得发愣。

items.cn: stupere 意为惊呆或麻木。

items.en: Stupid described a foolish person or act.
